title: Dirac scattering and the non-linear Fourier transform
summary: Carathéodory linear systems with integrable coefficients and a holomorphic parameter; half-plane function theory (Poisson integrals, Fatou, bounded holomorphic functions, H², Paley–Wiener, outer functions); Dirac systems with locally integrable complex potential, their fundamental matrix and Hermite–Biehler functions; finite-interval SU(1,1) scattering with the half-plane inequality, outerness and the non-linear Plancherel identity (constant π/2); the square-integrable scattering limit and the non-linear Fourier transform with boundary values, Plancherel at infinity and L² convergence of truncations; de Branges spaces, Weyl functions, spectral measures and the Szegő condition; meromorphic inner functions and resonances; universality and approximation of Hermite–Biehler functions; Poltoratski's pointwise convergence theorem for real square-integrable potentials.

layers.title: Carathéodory linear systems with a holomorphic parameter

targets.name: le_mul_exp_integral_of_le_add_integral
targets.statement: Let `a ≤ b`, let `β : ℝ → ℝ` be nonnegative and integrable on `[a, b]`, let `α ∈ ℝ`, and let `u : ℝ → ℝ` be measurable and bounded on `[a, b]` with `u(t) ≤ α + ∫ₐᵗ β u` for every `t ∈ [a, b]`. Prove that `u(t) ≤ α exp(∫ₐᵗ β)` for every `t ∈ [a, b]`, and the backward form on `[a, b]` with `∫ₜᵇ`. Route: `v(t) = ∫ₐᵗ β u` is absolutely continuous with `v′ = βu ≤ αβ + βv` almost everywhere, so `(v e^{−∫ₐᵗβ})′ ≤ αβ e^{−∫ₐᵗβ}` almost everywhere; integrate with the constancy theorem (coddingtonlevinson1955, Ch. 1, waived; the constant-kernel case is Tau Ceti `TauCeti.le_mul_exp_of_le_add_mul_integral`).

locator.where: Ch. 1 (Grönwall's inequality), waived; constant-kernel case Tau Ceti TauCeti.le_mul_exp_of_le_add_mul_integral

targets.name: existsUnique_caratheodory_linear
targets.statement: Let `a ≤ b`, `t₀ ∈ [a, b]`, `y₀ ∈ E`, let `P` be a coefficient on `[a, b]` and let `F : ℝ → E` be integrable on `[a, b]`. Prove that there is exactly one `Y : ℝ → E`, continuous on `[a, b]`, with `Y(t) = y₀ + ∫_{t₀}^{t} (P(s)Y(s) + F(s)) ds` for every `t ∈ [a, b]`. Prove that this `Y` is absolutely continuous on `[a, b]`, has derivative `P(t)Y(t) + F(t)` at almost every `t ∈ (a, b)`, and satisfies `‖Y(t)‖ ≤ (‖y₀‖ + |∫_{t₀}^{t} ‖F‖|) exp|∫_{t₀}^{t} ‖P‖|`; conversely an absolutely continuous `Y` with `Y(t₀) = y₀` and derivative `P Y + F` almost everywhere is this solution. Route: Picard iteration in `C([a, b], E)`, where the `n`-th iterate moves two curves at time `t` by at most `(∫_{t₀}^{t}‖P‖)ⁿ/n!` times their distance, so that some iterate is a contraction; uniqueness by 1.1 (coddingtonlevinson1955, Ch. 2 §1, waived; romanov2014 line 212–224 for the canonical-system case).
hypotheses: P a.e. strongly measurable with ‖P‖ integrable on [a,b]

targets.name: caratheodoryPropagator

targets.name: det_caratheodoryPropagator
targets.statement: For `E = Fin n → 𝕜` or `E = EuclideanSpace 𝕜 (Fin n)` and a matrix coefficient `P`, prove `det N_P(t, s) = exp(∫_s^t tr P)` for `s, t ∈ I`, with `N_P(t, s)` and `P(r)` identified with their matrices in the standard basis (coddingtonlevinson1955, Ch. 1 §7, waived; romanov2014 line 218–219 for `det ≡ 1`). Route: fix `s`. At almost every `t` the curve `N_P(·, s)` has derivative `P(t)N` at `t`, where `N = N_P(t, s)` is invertible (§1.2, §1.3). The chain rule and Jacobi's formula at an invertible matrix (Tau Ceti `Matrix.hasFDerivAt_det`, restricted to real scalars when `𝕜 = ℂ`) then give `∂ₜ det N_P(t, s) = det N · tr(N⁻¹P(t)N) = det N · tr P(t)`. Each entry `N ↦ (N e_j)_i` is `1`-Lipschitz on `E →L[𝕜] E`, since `|(N e_j)_i| ≤ ‖N e_j‖ ≤ ‖N‖`. So the entries of the absolutely continuous curve `N_P(·, s)` (§1.2) are absolutely continuous (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.comp_absolutelyContinuousOnInterval`). The function `det N_P(·, s)` is then absolutely continuous, being a finite sum of products of these entries (the Leibniz expansion). It is therefore an absolutely continuous solution of the scalar equation `y′ = (tr P) y`, `y(s) = 1`, whose coefficient is integrable because `|tr P| ≤ n‖P‖`. By the uniqueness clause of §1.2 it equals `exp(∫_s^t tr P)`, which solves the same equation. The same formula holds for `E = EuclideanSpace 𝕜 (Fin n)`, the carrier of §3.1. Mathlib's `EuclideanSpace.equiv` is a continuous linear equivalence with `Fin n → 𝕜` that is the identity on coordinates. Conjugation by it carries a coefficient to a coefficient, and so, by the uniqueness clause of §1.2, the propagator to the propagator. It changes neither the matrices in the standard basis nor their determinants and traces.
hypotheses: E = Fin n → 𝕜 or E = EuclideanSpace 𝕜 (Fin n)
P a matrix coefficient on I

targets.name: differentiableOn_caratheodoryPropagator
targets.statement: Let `E` be a complex Banach space, `U ⊆ ℂ` open, and `P : ℝ × ℂ → (E →L[ℂ] E)` such that `t ↦ P(t, z)` is a coefficient on `I` for each `z ∈ U`, `z ↦ P(t, z)` is holomorphic on `U` for almost every `t ∈ I`, and for every compact `K ⊆ U` there is `m_K` integrable on compact subintervals of `I` with `‖P(t, z)‖ ≤ m_K(t)` for `z ∈ K` and almost every `t`. Prove that for `s, t ∈ I` the map `z ↦ N_{P(·,z)}(t, s)` is holomorphic on `U`, that `(t, s, z) ↦ N_{P(·,z)}(t, s)` is continuous on `I × I × U`, that `z ↦ N_{P(·,z)}(·, s)` is holomorphic from `U` into `C(J, E →L[ℂ] E)` for every compact `J ⊆ I`, with `‖N_{P(·,z)}(t, s)‖ ≤ exp|∫_s^t m_K|` for `z ∈ K`, and that `∂_z N(t, s) = ∫_s^t N(t, r) ∂_z P(r, z) N(r, s) dr`. In particular an entire coefficient (`U = ℂ`) gives entire propagators (romanov2014 line 220–222; coddingtonlevinson1955, Ch. 1 §7, waived). Route: each Dyson term is a parametric integral of a holomorphic integrand dominated on compacts, hence holomorphic, and the series converges locally uniformly.
hypotheses: t ↦ P(t,z) a coefficient for z ∈ U
z ↦ P(t,z) holomorphic for a.e. t
locally uniform integrable domination on compacts K ⊆ U

In the maximum-row-sum norm of `Fin 2 → ℂ` the coefficient at `z = 0` has norm `|f(t)| + |g(t)|`, which exceeds `|q(t)|` whenever `f(t)g(t) ≠ 0`: for `q = 1 + i` it is `2 > √2 = |q|`. At a fixed `z` the conclusion is the fixed-parameter existence statement of 1.2.

targets.name: existsUnique_caratheodory
targets.statement: Let `t₀ ∈ I`, `x₀ ∈ E` and `F : ℝ × E → E` with `t ↦ F(t, x)` strongly measurable on `I` for each `x`, `‖F(t, x) − F(t, y)‖ ≤ L(t)‖x − y‖` and `‖F(t, x₀)‖ ≤ m(t)` for almost every `t ∈ I` and all `x, y`, where `L, m ≥ 0` are integrable on compact subintervals of `I`. Prove that there is exactly one `Y` continuous on `I` with `Y(t) = x₀ + ∫_{t₀}^{t} F(s, Y(s)) ds` for `t ∈ I`; that it is absolutely continuous on compact subintervals with `‖Y(t) − x₀‖ ≤ |∫_{t₀}^{t} m| exp|∫_{t₀}^{t} L|`; and that two initial values give solutions at distance at most `‖x₀ − x₀′‖ exp|∫_{t₀}^{t} L|`. Prove the local form: if the two bounds hold only for `x, y` in the closed ball of radius `r` about `x₀` and for `t` in `[t₀, t₀ + δ] ⊆ I`, there is a unique solution on `[t₀, t₀ + τ]` for every `τ ≤ δ` with `(∫_{t₀}^{t₀+τ} m) exp(∫_{t₀}^{t₀+τ} L) ≤ r`. The composite `s ↦ F(s, Y(s))` is strongly measurable because `Y` is a uniform limit of step functions and `F` is Lipschitz in `x` (coddingtonlevinson1955, Ch. 2 §1, waived).
hypotheses: L, m ≥ 0 locally integrable on I

layers.title: Function theory of the upper half-plane

targets.name: poissonIntegral
targets.statement: Define the Poisson kernel `P(z, x)` for `z ∈ ℂ₊`, `x ∈ ℝ` as Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.halfSpacePoissonKernel 2 v` with unit inward normal `v = (0, 1)`, pole `z` and boundary point `x`, read through Mathlib's `Complex.orthonormalBasisOneI`; since `⟨v, z⟩ = Im z` and `2ω₂ = 2π` (Mathlib `EuclideanSpace.volume_ball_fin_two`), it is `P(z, x) = Im z/(π|x − z|²)`, the notation used below. Define the Poisson measure `Π = dx/(1 + x²)`; a positive Borel measure `ν` on `ℝ` is Poisson-finite when `∫ dν/(1 + x²) < ∞`. Define the Poisson integral `P[ν](z) = ∫ P(z, x) dν(x)`, and for a complex `h ∈ L¹(Π)` write `P[h] = P[h dx]` (componentwise). For a Poisson-finite `ν` (or a real `h ∈ L¹(Π)`) define the Schwarz integral `S[ν](z) = (1/(πi)) ∫ (1/(x − z) − x/(1 + x²)) dν(x)`, and for `h ∈ L¹(ℝ)` the integral normalised at infinity `S⁰[h](z) = (1/(πi)) ∫ h(x)/(x − z) dx` (poltoratski2024 line 250–254 and 610–614; mauth2022 line 378–392).
hypotheses: ν a Poisson-finite positive Borel measure on ℝ (or h ∈ L¹(Π))

api.name: andWithSoIs
api.statement: `∫ P(z, x) dx = 1` (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.integral_halfSpacePoissonKernel`; the hyperplane carries the Lebesgue measure of `ℝ` by Mathlib `LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving`), and `P(z, x) ≤ C(z)/(1 + x²)` with `C(z) = 2(1 + (Re z)²) max(Im z, 1/Im z)/π`, so `P[ν]` is finite on `ℂ₊` for Poisson-finite `ν`.

api.name: isHarmonicOnNonnegative
api.statement: `P[ν]` is harmonic on `ℂ₊`, nonnegative, and `P[ν] = Re S[ν]`; `S[ν]` is holomorphic on `ℂ₊` and real at `z = i`; `S⁰[h] − S[h]` is the imaginary constant `−(i/π) ∫ x h(x)/(1 + x²) dx`. Route: on a compact subset of `ℂ₊` the `z`-derivative `(x − z)^{−2}` of the Schwarz integrand is bounded by a constant times `1/(1 + x²)`, so `S[ν]` is holomorphic (Mathlib `hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le`), hence analytic (Mathlib `DifferentiableOn.analyticAt`). Its real part `P[ν]` is then harmonic (Mathlib `AnalyticAt.harmonicAt_re`). It is nonnegative because the kernel is positive (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.halfSpacePoissonKernel_pos`).

api.name: soExactlyWhen
api.statement: `P(i, x) = 1/(π(1 + x²))`, so `h ∈ L¹(Π)` exactly when `P[|h|](i) < ∞`.

api.name: cayleyComparisonWithAnd
api.statement: Cayley comparison: with `w = (z − i)/(z + i)` and `ζ = (x − i)/(x + i)`, `P(z, x) = poissonKernel 0 w ζ · 1/(π(1 + x²))`, where Mathlib's disc Poisson kernel is `poissonKernel 0 w ζ = (1 − |w|²)/|ζ − w|²` for `|ζ| = 1`. So `P[ν](z) = ∫ poissonKernel 0 w ζ dσ(ζ)` is the disc Poisson integral at `w` of the image `σ` of `dν/(π(1 + x²))` under Tau Ceti `TauCeti.boundaryCayley`.

api.name: translationAndDilationCovariance
api.statement: Translation and dilation covariance: for the translate `ν_u` of `ν` by `u ∈ ℝ`, `P[ν_u](z) = P[ν](z − u)`; for `λ > 0` and the image `ν^λ` of `ν` under `x ↦ x/λ`, `P[ν^λ](z) = λ P[ν](λz)`.

tests.name: identificationWithThePinnedKernel
tests.statement: Identification with the pinned kernel: at `z = 1 + i` and `x = 3`, Tau Ceti's kernel at `n = 2`, `v = (0, 1)`, with pole `z` is `2 · 1/(2π · 5) = 1/(5π)`, which is `Im z/(π|x − z|²)`. With the two arguments exchanged (pole `x`) it is `0`, because `⟨v, x⟩ = 0` for real `x`.

This `h` is real, bounded and continuous, so `P[h]` is also Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.halfSpacePoissonIntegral` at `n = 2`, harmonic by `TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_halfSpacePoissonIntegral`.

For `h(x) = (x² − 1)/(x² + 1) = Re ζ`, Mathlib's Poisson formula on the unit disc (`InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.circleAverage_poissonKernel_smul` for the harmonic function `Re`) gives `P[h](z) = Re w`. At `z = 2i` the direct integral is `(2/π)∫ (x² − 1)/((x² + 1)(x² + 4)) dx = 1/3 = Re(1/3)`. A kernel that also carried the circle-average factor `1/(2π)` would give `1/(6π)`.

I §3, uncertified). Route: `u = Im F` with `F` holomorphic on `ℂ₊`, `F′` being the conjugate complex partial of `u`, which is holomorphic by Mathlib's `HarmonicAt.differentiableAt_complex_partial` and has a primitive by Tau Ceti `DifferentiableOn.hasDerivAt_wedgeIntegral_upperHalfPlane`; then Tau Ceti `TauCeti.exists_isFiniteMeasure_eq_nevanlinnaKernel_add` and `TauCeti.nevanlinnaKernel_im` give `u = β Im z + P[ν]` with `ν = π(1 + x²)ρ`. Uniqueness: `ν` is the vague limit of the measures `u(x + iy) dx` as `y → 0`, and `c = lim u(iy)/y` as `y → ∞`.

tests.name: isHarmonicButTakes
tests.statement: `u = Re z` is harmonic but takes the value `−1` at `−1 + i`; positivity is a hypothesis.

targets.name: nontangentialMaximal
targets.statement: For `x ∈ ℝ` and `0 < h ≤ ∞` define the cone `Γ_h(x) = {z ∈ ℂ₊ : |Re z − x| < Im z < h}` and, for `u : ℂ₊ → ℂ`, the nontangential maximal function `M_h u(x) = sup_{z ∈ Γ_h(x)} |u(z)|` with values in `[0, ∞]`. A function has nontangential limit `L` at `x` when it tends to `L` along the filter of `Γ_∞(x)` at `x` (poltoratski2024 line 615–622; mauth2022 line 411–420; garnett2007, Ch. I §§4–5, pp. 27, 55–56, uncertified). Its API:
hypotheses: h ∈ L¹(Π) (bounded-cone bounds), g ∈ L²(ℝ) (L² bound)

locator.where: Lemmas 5–6, Corollary 1, line 411–433; poltoratski2024 line 615–622; garnett2007 Ch. I §§4–5 (uncertified)

api.name: coneComparisonForAnd
api.statement: Cone comparison: for `x′ + iy ∈ Γ_∞(x)` and every `s ∈ ℝ`, `P(x′ + iy, s) ≤ 3 P(x + iy, s)`; hence for `g` locally integrable with `P[|g|]` finite, `M_∞ P[g](x) ≤ 3 · TauCeti.maximalFunction volume g x`. The kernel inequality is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.halfSpacePoissonKernel_le_mul` at `n = 2` with the poles `x′ + iy` and `x + iy` of equal height and `A = √3`, so that `Aⁿ = 3`.

api.name: apertureIndependenceConesGive
api.statement: Aperture independence: cones `|Re z − x| < α Im z`, `α > 0`, give the same nontangential limits, by the same comparison with `A² = max(2, 1 + 2α²)`, which is `3` for `α = 1`.

api.name: localisationForAndThere
api.statement: Localisation: for `h ∈ L¹(Π)` and `R > 0` there is `C_R`, depending only on `R`, with `M_1 P[h](x) ≤ 3 · TauCeti.maximalFunction volume (h · 1_{[−R−2, R+2]}) x + C_R ‖h‖_{L¹(Π)}` for `|x| ≤ R`.

api.name: weakTypeForSo
api.statement: Weak type: `|{x ∈ [−R, R] : M_1 P[h](x) > λ}| ≤ C_R ‖h‖_{L¹(Π)}/λ` for `λ > 0`, so `√(M_1 P[|h|])` is integrable on every bounded interval (mauth2022 Lemma 5 and Corollary 1, line 421–427).

api.name: strongTypeForWith
api.statement: Strong type: `‖M_∞ P[g]‖_{L²} ≤ C‖g‖_{L²}` for `g ∈ L²(ℝ)` with an absolute constant `C` (mauth2022 Lemma 6 line 430).

api.name: routeGivesIsRadially
api.statement: Route: `|s − x| ≤ |s − x′| + y` gives `(s − x)² + y² ≤ 3((s − x′)² + y²)`, which is the distance hypothesis `|s − (x + iy)| ≤ √3 |s − (x′ + iy)|` of the pinned comparison. `P(x + iy, ·)` is radially decreasing about `x` with integral `1` (§2.1), so its integral against `|g|` is at most the maximal function by the layer-cake formula; then Tau Ceti's weak and strong type bounds.

tests.name: andWhileTheMaximal
tests.statement: `h = 1_{[0,1]}` and `x = 2`: `P[h](2 + i) = (arctan 2 − π/4)/π ≈ 0.102`, while the maximal function of `h` at `2` is `1/4` (attained at radius `2`), and `0.102 ≤ 3 · 1/4`.

tests.name: theConstantAtAnd
tests.statement: The constant `3`: at `x = 0`, `z = 0.99 + i ∈ Γ_∞(0)` and `s = 1`, `P(0.99 + i, 1) = 1/(1.0001π)` and `3P(i, 1) = 3/(2π)`, so the inequality holds; at `s = 2` the ratio is `P(0.99 + i, 2)/P(i, 2) = 5/2.0201 ≈ 2.475`. Over the open cone the ratio `P(x′ + iy, s)/P(iy, s)` has supremum `(s² + y²)/((s − y)² + y²)` for `s ≥ y`, largest at `s = y(1 + √5)/2` with value `((1 + √5)/2)² ≈ 2.618`, not attained; so no constant below `2.618` works, and `3` is not sharp. The point `1 + i` lies on the boundary of `Γ_∞(0)`, not in it.

tests.name: bothMaximalFunctionsVanish
tests.statement: `h = 0`: both maximal functions vanish; `h ≡ 1` (in `L¹(Π)`, not in `L¹`): `P[h] ≡ 1` and `M_1 P[h] ≡ 1`.

tests.name: theGlobalMaximalFunction
tests.statement: The global maximal function of `h ∈ L¹(Π)` can be infinite (for `h ≡ 1` the averages over `B(x, r)` stay `1`, but for `h(x) = |x|^{1/2}` they grow like `√r`), which is why the bound is localised to `[−R − 2, R + 2]` with a tail term.

targets.name: ae_tendsto_poissonIntegral_nontangential
targets.statement: Let `ν` be Poisson-finite with Lebesgue decomposition `ν = w dx + ν_s`. Prove that for almost every `x ∈ ℝ`, `P[ν](z) → w(x)` as `z → x` nontangentially; in particular `P[ν_s] → 0` nontangentially almost everywhere, and `P[h] → h(x)` nontangentially at almost every `x` for complex `h ∈ L¹(Π)` (mauth2022 Lemmas 4 and 7, line 404–436; garnett2007, Ch. I §§3–5, pp. 16, 30, uncertified). Route: at a Lebesgue point of `w` where `ν_s(B(x, r))/2r → 0` (Mathlib `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div` and `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv`), split `ν − w(x)dx` near and far from `x` and use the cone domination of §2.3.
hypotheses: ν Poisson-finite with Lebesgue decomposition w dx + ν_s

locator.where: Lemmas 4 and 7, line 404–436; garnett2007 Ch. I §§3–5 pp. 16, 30 (uncertified)

tests.name: theLimitIsAt
tests.statement: `ν = δ₀`: the limit is `0` at every `x ≠ 0`, and `w = 0`.

tests.name: theLimitIsOn
tests.statement: `h = 1_{[0,1]}`: the limit is `1` on `(0, 1)` and `0` off `[0, 1]`; at the jump `x = 0` there is no nontangential limit, since `P[h](iy) → 1/2` while `P[h](−y/2 + iy) → 1/2 − arctan(1/2)/π ≈ 0.352`.

tests.name: continuousBoundedTheLimit
tests.statement: Continuous bounded `h`: the limit exists at every point and equals `h(x)`, even without restriction on the approach; this is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.tendsto_halfSpacePoissonIntegral` at `n = 2`, applied to `Re h` and `Im h`.

targets.name: boundaryFunction
targets.statement: For `F` holomorphic and bounded on `ℂ₊` define its boundary function `F* ∈ L^∞(ℝ)` as the nontangential limit of `F`, which exists almost everywhere (garnett2007, Ch. II §§1–4, pp. 55, 64, uncertified). Its API:
hypotheses: F holomorphic and bounded on ℂ₊

api.name: andOnIsLinear
api.statement: `‖F*‖_∞ ≤ sup_{ℂ₊} |F|` and `F = P[F*]` on `ℂ₊`; `F ↦ F*` is linear and multiplicative.

api.name: ifExtendsContinuouslyTo
api.statement: If `F` extends continuously to the closed half-plane then `F* = F` on `ℝ`.

api.name: uniquenessIfVanishesOn
api.statement: Uniqueness: if `F*` vanishes on a set of positive measure then `F ≡ 0`.

api.name: ifThenAndOn
api.statement: If `F ≢ 0` then `log|F*| ∈ L¹(Π)` and `log|F(z)| ≤ P[log|F*|](z)` on `ℂ₊`.

api.name: routeTheBoundedFunctions
api.statement: Route: the bounded functions `F(· + iε)` are continuous up to `ℝ`. The Poisson integral of their restriction to `ℝ` is harmonic and tends to `F(x + iε)` at every `x ∈ ℝ` (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_halfSpacePoissonIntegral` and `TauCeti.tendsto_halfSpacePoissonIntegral`, for the real and imaginary parts). So `F(· + iε) − P[F(· + iε)|_ℝ]`, reflected oddly across `ℝ`, is continuous, has the mean-value property (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_of_setAverage_ball_eq`) and is bounded, hence constant by `InnerProductSpace.bounded_harmonic_on_complex_plane_is_constant`, hence `0`. A weak-* limit point of `F(· + iε)` in `L^∞(Π) = L¹(Π)^*` gives the Poisson representation, because `x ↦ (1 + x²)P(z, x)` is bounded and so lies in `L¹(Π)`; as a space of classes `L^∞(Π)` is `L^∞(ℝ)`, since `Π` and Lebesgue measure have the same null sets. §2.4 then gives the nontangential limits. Uniqueness and the logarithmic bound transport Tau Ceti `TauCeti.eqOn_const_ball_of_tendsto_circleMap` and `AnalyticOnNhd.le_circleAverage_log_norm` through the Cayley transform, under which a disc radius ending at `ζ ≠ 1` becomes an arc ending at `x` inside every cone at `x`. Jensen's bound is stated at the centre of the disc. It gives the logarithmic bound at `z = i`, because the Cayley transform carries `P(i, x) dx` to `dθ/(2π)`: this is §2.1's Cayley comparison at `w = 0`, where `poissonKernel 0 0 ζ = 1`. §2.1's translation and dilation covariance, applied to `F(Re z + (Im z) ·)`, then give the bound at every `z ∈ ℂ₊`.

tests.name: isBoundedByNot
tests.statement: `F(z) = e^{−i/z}` is bounded by `1` (`|F| = e^{−Im z/|z|²}`), not continuous at `0`, and `F* = e^{−i/x}` still has `P[F*] = F`.

targets.name: HardySpaceUpper
targets.statement: Define `H²(ℂ₊)` as the holomorphic `F` on `ℂ₊` with `‖F‖² = sup_{y>0} ∫ |F(x + iy)|² dx < ∞` (mauth2022 line 337–358). Its API:

locator.where: line 337–358, Lemmas 1, 2, 6, 9, 11; garnett2007 p. 84 and Ch. II §4 (uncertified)

api.name: boundaryValuesInAs
api.statement: Boundary values: `F(· + iy) → F*` in `L²(ℝ)` as `y → 0`, `‖F*‖_{L²} = ‖F‖`, `y ↦ ‖F(· + iy)‖_{L²}` is nonincreasing, `F → F*` nontangentially almost everywhere, and `F = P[F*]` (mauth2022 Lemma 1 line 359–369, for `H^p(ℂ₊)` with `1 < p < ∞`; garnett2007, Ch. II p. 55, uncertified).

api.name: paleyWienerTheBoundary
api.statement: Paley–Wiener: the boundary map is an isometry of `H²(ℂ₊)` onto `{g ∈ L²(ℝ) : 𝓕g = 0 almost everywhere on (−∞, 0)}` (Mathlib's `𝓕`), and `F(z) = ∫₀^∞ φ(s) e^{isz} ds` with `φ ∈ L²(0, ∞)`, `‖F‖² = 2π‖φ‖²` (mauth2022 Lemma 9 line 469; garnett2007 p. 84, uncertified); in particular `H²(ℂ₊)` is a Hilbert space.

api.name: cauchyFormulaAndFor
api.statement: Cauchy formula: `F(z) = (1/(2πi)) ∫ F*(x)/(x − z) dx` and `∫ F*(x)/(x − conj z) dx = 0` for `z ∈ ℂ₊`; hence `|F(z)|² ≤ ‖F‖²/(4π Im z)` (mauth2022 Lemma 2 line 370–377 states a weaker constant).

api.name: productsForBoundedMultipliers
api.statement: Products: `∫ F*(x) G*(x) dx = 0` for `F, G ∈ H²(ℂ₊)`; bounded multipliers: `GF ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` with `‖GF‖ ≤ sup|G| ‖F‖` for bounded holomorphic `G`.

api.name: logarithmicBound
api.statement: Logarithmic bound: if `F ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` and `F ≢ 0`, then `log|F*| ∈ L¹(Π)`, so `F* ≠ 0` almost everywhere, and `log|F(z)| ≤ P[log|F*|](z)` for every `z ∈ ℂ₊` (garnett2007, Ch. II §4, uncertified). Route: for `ε > 0` the translate `F(· + iε)` is holomorphic near the closed half-plane and bounded there by `‖F‖/√(4πε)` (the point bound above). So §2.5 gives the bound for it, with boundary function `F(· + iε)` on `ℝ`. As `ε → 0`, `log⁺|F(· + iε)| → log⁺|F*|` in `L¹(P(z, x) dx)`. This is because `|log⁺a − log⁺b| ≤ |a − b|` for `a, b ≥ 0`, `F(· + iε) → F*` in `L²(ℝ)`, and `∫ P(z, x)² dx = 1/(2π Im z)`. Take a sequence `εₙ → 0` along which `F(· + iεₙ) → F*` almost everywhere. Fatou's lemma for `log⁻|F(· + iεₙ)|` then gives the bound in the limit at every `z` with `F(z) ≠ 0`. At one such `z` it also gives the integrability of `log⁻|F*|`, while `log⁺|F*| ≤ |F*|²` is integrable.

api.name: weakConvergenceInImplies
api.statement: Weak convergence `Fₙ ⇀ F` in `H²(ℂ₊)` implies locally uniform convergence on `ℂ₊` (mauth2022 Lemma 11 line 487), and `‖M_∞ F‖_{L²} ≤ C‖F‖` (mauth2022 Lemma 6, via §2.3).

api.name: isDefinedByReflection
api.statement: `H²(ℂ₋)` is defined by reflection, and its boundary values are the complex conjugates of those of `H²(ℂ₊)`, orthogonal to them in `L²(ℝ)`.

tests.name: andThePointBound
tests.statement: `F(z) = 1/(z + i)`: `F(z) = −i∫₀^∞ e^{−s} e^{isz} ds`, `‖F‖² = π`, and the point bound at `z = i` is attained: `|F(i)|² = 1/4 = π/(4π)`.

tests.name: theProductOfWith
tests.statement: `∫ dx/(x + i)² = 0`: the product of `1/(z + i)` with itself, as the product law requires.

tests.name: logarithmicBoundEqualityAndStrictCases
tests.statement: Logarithmic bound, equality and strict cases: for `F = 1/(z + i)`, `log|F*| = −log|x + i|` and `P[log|F*|](z) = −log|z + i| = log|F(z)|` (the outer case of §2.8; at `z = i` both sides are `−log 2 ≈ −0.693`). For `F = e^{iz}/(z + i)` the boundary modulus is the same, but `log|F(z)|` is smaller by `Im z`: at `z = i` it is `−1 − log 2 ≈ −1.693 < −0.693`. For `F ≡ 0` the boundary function `log|F*|` is identically `−∞`, so `F ≢ 0` is needed.

tests.name: isNotInThe
tests.statement: `F ≡ 1` is not in `H²(ℂ₊)` (the integrals are infinite), and `1/(z − i)` is not holomorphic on `ℂ₊`.

tests.name: mathlibConventionWitnessFor
tests.statement: Mathlib-convention witness: for `g(x) = 1/(x + i)`, closing the contour in the lower half-plane gives `𝓕g(w) = −2πi e^{−2πw}` for `w > 0`, and `𝓕g(w) = 0` for `w < 0`; the vanishing condition is on the negative frequencies, and a statement with `(0, ∞)` describes `H²(ℂ₋)`.

targets.name: paleyWiener
targets.statement: For `t ≥ 0` define `PW_t` as the set of `F : ℂ → ℂ` with `F(z) = ∫_{−t}^{t} φ(s) e^{isz} ds` for some `φ ∈ L²(−t, t)` (poltoratski2024 line 236–244; mauth2022 Lemma 10 line 472–484). Its API:

api.name: isEntireIsA
api.statement: `F` is entire, `|F(z)| ≤ √(2t) ‖φ‖ e^{t|Im z|}`, `‖F‖²_{L²(ℝ)} = 2π‖φ‖²`, `PW_t` is a closed subspace of `L²(ℝ)`, `PW_s ⊆ PW_t` for `s ≤ t`, and `F ∈ PW_t` implies `F# ∈ PW_t`.

api.name: andConverselyAnEntire
api.statement: `e^{itz}F ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` and `e^{−itz}F ∈ H²(ℂ₋)`; conversely an entire `H` with `e^{itz}H ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` and `e^{−itz}H ∈ H²(ℂ₋)` belongs to `PW_t` (mauth2022 Lemma 10).

api.name: paleyWienerTheoremAn
api.statement: Paley–Wiener theorem: an entire `F` of exponential type at most `t` (`|F(z)| ≤ C_ε e^{(t+ε)|z|}` for every `ε > 0`) whose restriction to `ℝ` is square-integrable belongs to `PW_t`.

api.name: reproducingKernelWithAnd
api.statement: Reproducing kernel: `F(λ) = ∫ F(x) conj(k_t(λ, x)) dx` with `k_t(λ, z) = sin(t(z − conj λ))/(π(z − conj λ))`, and `‖k_t(λ, ·)‖² = k_t(λ, λ) = sinh(2t Im λ)/(2π Im λ)`, equal to `t/π` for real `λ` (poltoratski2024 (2.3)–(2.4) line 241–249).

api.name: exactlyWhenIsAbsolutely
api.statement: `zF ∈ PW_t` exactly when `φ` is absolutely continuous on `[−t, t]` with `φ′ ∈ L²` and `φ(±t) = 0` (then `zF(z) = i∫ φ′(s) e^{isz} ds`); these `F` are dense in `PW_t`.

tests.name: and
tests.statement: `φ = 1_{[−t,t]}`: `F(z) = 2 sin(tz)/z`, and `‖F‖² = ∫ 4 sin²(tx)/x² dx = 4πt = 2π · 2t`.

tests.name: isEntireOfExponential
tests.statement: `e^{itz}` is entire of exponential type `t` but not square-integrable on `ℝ`, and `sin(tz)/z` lies in `PW_t` but not in `PW_s` for `s < t`.

tests.name: kernelNormNumericallyFor
tests.statement: Kernel norm: `∫ sin²(t(y − x))/(π²(y − x)²) dy = t/π` (numerically `0.63657` for `t = 2` against `2/π ≈ 0.63662`).

targets.name: outerFunction
targets.statement: For real `h ∈ L¹(Π)` define the outer function `O_h = exp(S[h])`, and for real `h ∈ L¹(ℝ)` the outer function normalised at infinity `O⁰_h = exp(S⁰[h])`. A holomorphic `F` on `ℂ₊` is outer when `F = c O_h` with `|c| = 1` and `h ∈ L¹(Π)`; `h` is its boundary log-modulus (mauth2022 line 454–468; garnett2007, Ch. II §4, p. 64, uncertified). Its API:
hypotheses: h real, h ∈ L¹(Π) (resp. L¹(ℝ) for the normalisation at infinity)

locator.where: line 454–468, Lemma 8; garnett2007 Ch. II §4 p. 64 (uncertified)

api.name: isHolomorphicAndZero
api.statement: `O_h` is holomorphic and zero-free on `ℂ₊` with `|O_h| = exp P[h]`; by §2.4 its nontangential boundary modulus is `e^{h(x)}` for almost every `x` (mauth2022 Lemma 8 line 463).

api.name: isBoundedExactlyWhen
api.statement: `O_h` is bounded exactly when `h` is essentially bounded above, with `sup |O_h| = e^{ess sup h}`.

api.name: aZeroFreeHolomorphic
api.statement: A zero-free holomorphic `F` on `ℂ₊` with `log|F| = P[h]` is `c O_h` with `|c| = 1`; two outer functions with the same boundary modulus differ by a unimodular constant.

api.name: forEvenIsReal
api.statement: For even `h`, `O_h` is real and positive on the imaginary axis.

api.name: outerMultipliers
api.statement: Outer multipliers: let `F ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` and let `G = c O_h` be outer with `|F*| e^h ∈ L²(ℝ)`. Then `FG ∈ H²(ℂ₊)`, `|(FG)*| = |F*| e^h` almost everywhere, and `‖FG‖ = ‖F* e^h‖_{L²}` (garnett2007, Ch. II §4, uncertified; poltoratski2024 line 685–687 and line 766 and mauth2022 line 945 and line 1137 use it without proof). Route: the case `F ≡ 0` is trivial. Otherwise the logarithmic bound of §2.6 and `log|G| = P[h]` give `2 log|FG(z)| ≤ P[k](z)` with `k = 2 log|F*| + 2h ∈ L¹(Π)`. Jensen's inequality for the probability measure `P(z, x) dx` and the convex function `exp` gives `|FG(z)|² ≤ P[|F*|² e^{2h}](z)`. Integrating in `x` at height `y`, with `∫ P(x + iy, u) dx = 1` and Tonelli, gives `∫ |FG(x + iy)|² dx ≤ ‖F* e^h‖²`. The boundary modulus follows from the nontangential limits of `F` (§2.6) and of `|G| = e^{P[h]}` (§2.4), and the norm identity from `‖FG‖ = ‖(FG)*‖_{L²}` (§2.6).

api.name: boundaryValuesOfOuterFunctions
api.statement: Boundary values of outer functions: if the measure `e^{2h} dx` is Poisson-finite (`∫ e^{2h} dΠ < ∞`), then `O_h/(z + i) ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` by the previous bullet with `F = 1/(z + i)`. So `O_h` has a nontangential limit at almost every `x ∈ ℝ` (§2.6), of modulus `e^{h(x)}`.

tests.name: soAndIsEven
tests.statement: `h(x) = log|x + i|`: `(1/π)∫ log(1 + x²)/(1 + x²) dx = 2 log 2`, so `O_h(i) = 2` and `O_h(z) = −i(z + i)`; `h` is even and `O_h(iy) = y + 1 > 0`.

tests.name: hasBoundaryModulusBut
tests.statement: `e^{iz}` has boundary modulus `1` but is not `c O_0 = c`, and `(z − i)/(z + i)` has a zero; neither is outer.

tests.name: item2
tests.statement: `h = 0`: `O_0 = 1`, and the outer-multiplier bullet reduces to `FG = cF` with `‖FG‖ = ‖F‖`.

tests.name: outerMultiplierComputation
tests.statement: Outer multipliers: for `F = 1/(z + i)²` and `h = log|x + i|` (`G = −i(z + i)`), `FG = −i/(z + i) ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` with `‖FG‖² = π`, and `‖F* e^h‖² = ∫ |x + i|²/|x + i|⁴ dx = ∫ dx/(1 + x²) = π`.

tests.name: boundaryConditionIsNeeded
tests.statement: The boundary condition is needed: `F = 1/(z + i)` with the same `G` has `|F*| e^h = |x + i|/|x + i| = 1`, not in `L²(ℝ)`, and indeed `FG = −i` is not in `H²(ℂ₊)`.

tests.name: outernessIsNeeded
tests.statement: Outerness is needed: `G = e^{−iz}` is zero-free with `|G| = 1` on `ℝ`, but `log|G(z)| = Im z > 0 = P[0](z)`, so it is not outer. For `F = 1/(z + i)`, `|F*| · 1 ∈ L²(ℝ)`, while `FG = e^{−iz}/(z + i)` has `∫ |FG(x + iy)|² dx = πe^{2y}/(y + 1)`, unbounded in `y`.

layers.title: Dirac systems and their Hermite–Biehler functions

targets.name: diracFundamentalMatrix
targets.statement: Define `Q_q(t) = [[g(t), f(t)], [f(t), −g(t)]]` and the fundamental matrix `M_q(t, z)`, `t ≥ 0`, `z ∈ ℂ`, as the propagator `N(t, 0)` (§1.3) on `E = EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)` of the coefficient `−Ω(z − Q_q(t))`, acting through `Matrix.toEuclideanCLM`. The coefficient is entire in `z`, with Euclidean operator norm `‖−Ω(z − Q_q(t))‖ ≤ ‖Ω‖(|z| + ‖Q_q(t)‖) = |z| + |q(t)|` (§1.6, Conventions). `M` is the matrix of `N(t, 0)` in the standard basis. Write `M = [[A, B], [C, D]]`, `Θ = (A, C)ᵀ`, `Φ = (B, D)ᵀ` (poltoratski2024 line 136–166; mauth2022 (5)–(6) line 546–563).

api.name: andIsEntireJointly
api.statement: `ΩM(t, z) = Ω + ∫₀ᵗ (z − Q_q(s)) M(s, z) ds`, `M(0, z) = 1`, and `M(t, ·)` is entire, jointly continuous in `(t, z)`.

api.name: theCoefficientIsTrace
api.statement: `det M(t, z) = 1` (§1.4, the coefficient is trace-free; poltoratski2024 (2.1) line 204; mauth2022 Lemma 14 line 565).

api.name: areRealEntireFor
api.statement: `M(t, conj z) = conj M(t, z)`: `A, B, C, D` are real entire, for every complex potential, because `Q_q` has real entries.

api.name: chainRuleForRomanov
api.statement: Chain rule: `M_q(t, z) = M_{q(s+·)}(t − s, z) M_q(s, z)` for `0 ≤ s ≤ t` (romanov2014 line 223–224), and locality: `M_q(t, ·)` depends only on `q` almost everywhere on `[0, t]`.

api.name: inParticularEveryEntry

targets.name: scatteringMatrix
targets.statement: Define the scattering matrix `G_q(t, z)` as the propagator `N(t, 0)` (§1.3) on `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)` of the coefficient `[[0, e^{−2izt} conj q(t)], [e^{2izt} q(t), 0]]`, entire in `z` with operator norm `max(|e^{−2izt}|, |e^{2izt}|) |q(t)| = |q(t)| e^{2t|Im z|}` (§1.6), and the scattering functions `a = (G_q)₂₂`, `b = (G_q)₂₁` (poltoratski2024 (5.3) line 492–501).

api.name: structureAndOnSo
api.statement: Structure: `G_q = [[a#, b#], [b, a]]` and `det G_q = a a# − b b# = 1`; on `ℝ`, `|a(t, x)|² − |b(t, x)|² = 1`, so `G_q(t, x) ∈ SU(1,1)` (poltoratski2024 line 501–503).

api.name: dictionaryWithEquivalentlyAnd
api.statement: Dictionary with §3.2: `a = e^{itz}(E + iẼ)/2`, `b = e^{itz}(E − iẼ)/2`, equivalently `E = e^{−itz}(a + b)` and `Ẽ = −i e^{−itz}(a − b)` (poltoratski2024 (5.2) line 484–488; mauth2022 line 187–189).

api.name: volterraFormAndPoltoratski
api.statement: Volterra form: `a(t, z) = 1 + ∫₀ᵗ q(s) e^{2izs} b#(s, z) ds` and `b(t, z) = ∫₀ᵗ q(s) e^{2izs} a#(s, z) ds` (poltoratski2024 (5.4) line 508–517).

api.name: localityDependsOnlyOn
api.statement: Locality: `G_q(t, ·)` depends only on `q` almost everywhere on `[0, t]`; if `q = 0` on `(T, t)` then `G_q(t, ·) = G_q(T, ·)`.

api.name: concatenationForWithAnd
api.statement: Concatenation: for `0 ≤ s ≤ t`, with `(a₁, b₁) = (a_q(s, ·), b_q(s, ·))` and `(a₂, b₂)` the scattering functions of `q(s + ·)` at time `t − s`, `b_q(t) = e^{2izs} b₂ a₁# + a₂ b₁` and `a_q(t) = e^{2izs} b₂ b₁# + a₂ a₁`.

api.name: translationOfThePotential
api.statement: Translation of the potential: for `t₀ ≥ 0` and `q^{t₀}(s) = q(s − t₀) 1_{s ≥ t₀}`, `a_{q^{t₀}}(t + t₀, z) = a_q(t, z)` and `b_{q^{t₀}}(t + t₀, z) = e^{2izt₀} b_q(t, z)`.

api.name: modulationOfThePotential
api.statement: Modulation of the potential: for `ξ ∈ ℝ`, `G_{q e^{2iξ·}}(t, z) = G_q(t, z + ξ)`.

api.name: dilationFor
api.statement: Dilation: for `λ > 0`, `G_{λ q(λ·)}(t, z) = G_q(λt, z/λ)`.

api.name: realPotentialsAndAnd
api.statement: Real potentials: `a(t, −conj z) = conj a(t, z)` and `b(t, −conj z) = conj b(t, z)`; `a(t, iy)` and `b(t, iy)` are real, and `a(t, 0) = cosh F(t)`, `b(t, 0) = sinh F(t)` with `F(t) = ∫₀ᵗ f`.

tests.name: positionOfForThe

tests.statement: Translation: for `q(s) = 0.4 cos 5s + 0.3i` on `[0, 1]`, `t₀ = 0.6`, `z = 0.3 + 0.1i`, the translated potential gives `a` equal to `a_q(1, z)` and `b` equal to `e^{2izt₀} b_q(1, z)` up to the discretisation error.

targets.name: norm_scatteringA_le_cosh
targets.statement: Let `L = ∫₀ᵗ |q|`. Prove that for `z` in the closed upper half-plane `|a(t, z)| ≤ cosh L`, `|a(t, z) − 1| ≤ cosh L − 1`, `|b(t, z)| ≤ sinh L` and `|b(t, z) − ∫₀ᵗ q(s) e^{2izs} ds| ≤ sinh L − L`; that `a(t, z) → 1` and `b(t, z) → 0` as `|z| → ∞` in the closed half-plane; and that for `q` integrable on `[0, ∞)` the functions `a(t, ·)`, `b(t, ·)` converge uniformly on the closed half-plane as `t → ∞`. Route: the `n`-th Dyson term of `a` or `b` is an integral over the simplex `s₁ < ⋯ < sₙ < t` of `q(sₙ) conj q(sₙ₋₁) ⋯` times `e^{2izσ}` with an alternating sum `σ ≥ 0`, so it is bounded by `Lⁿ/n!`; decay is the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma for the image of the simplex integrand under `σ`, uniform over the compact family `e^{−2σ Im z}`. For the discrete analogue on `ℓ¹`, see taothiele2012 Lecture 1 §3: Lemma 5 (line 430–433) gives the uniform convergence of truncations, and line 460–465 gives the bound `sup arccosh|a| ≤ Σ arccosh((1 − |F_n|²)^{−1/2})` on the circle.
hypotheses: q integrable on [0,t] (on [0,∞) for the uniform limit)

locator.where: Lecture 1 §3 Lemma 5 line 430–433 and line 460–465 (discrete analogue on ℓ¹)

tests.name: onTheOpenLower
tests.statement: On the open lower half-plane no bound holds: `|a(1, −5i)| ≈ 237`.

targets.name: one_le_normSq_scatteringA_sub_normSq_scatteringB
targets.statement: Prove that `|a(t, z)|² − |b(t, z)|² ≥ 1` for every `z` in the closed upper half-plane, with equality on `ℝ`; hence `|a(t, z)| ≥ 1`, `|b(t, z)| < |a(t, z)|`, `a(t, ·)` has no zeros in the closed half-plane, and `ρ(t, ·) = b(t, ·)/a(t, ·)` is holomorphic on a neighbourhood of the closed half-plane with `1 − |ρ(t, z)|² ≥ 1/|a(t, z)|²` (poltoratski2024 line 503–507; taothiele2012 Lemma 3 line 296 for the discrete model). Route: for `X = M(·, z)c`, `h(X) = Im(conj u · v)` satisfies `∂ₜh = Im z |X|² ≥ 2 Im z h` and `|u − iv|² − |u + iv|² = 4h`. For `c = c₁(1, i) + c₂(1, −i)` one has `h(c) = |c₁|² − |c₂|²`, `u − iv = 2e^{−itz}(c₁a + c₂b)` and `u + iv = 2e^{itz}(c₁b# + c₂a#)`, so `|c₁ a + c₂ b|² ≥ |c₁|² − |c₂|²` whenever `|c₂| ≤ |c₁|`; minimising over `c₂` gives `|a|² ≥ 1 + |b|²`.

tests.name: constantPotentialsOnAnd
tests.statement: Constant potentials `q ∈ {1, 0.3 + 2i, 3}` on `[0, 1]` and `z` on a grid of the closed half-plane give `min(|a|² − |b|²) = 1.0000` (attained on `ℝ`) and `min |a| ≈ 1.006`.

tests.name: realAt

tests.name: theInequalityFailsIn
tests.statement: The inequality fails in the lower half-plane: `q = 1` on `[0, 1]` at `z = −5i` gives `|a| ≈ 237 < |b| ≈ 2385`.

targets.name: integral_log_norm_scatteringA
targets.statement: Let `q` be square-integrable on `[0, t]`. Prove that `log a(t, ·)` (the logarithm vanishing at `i∞`) is a bounded holomorphic function on `ℂ₊`, that `y(a(t, iy) − 1) → ½∫₀ᵗ |q|²` as `y → ∞`, and the non-linear Plancherel identity `∫_ℝ log|a(t, x)| dx = (π/2) ∫₀ᵗ |q|²`; hence `log|a(t, ·)| ∈ L¹(ℝ)`, `a(t, ·) = O⁰_{log|a(t,·)|}` is outer, `log(1 − |ρ(t, x)|²) = −2 log|a(t, x)|` on `ℝ`, and `∫ −log(1 − |ρ(t, x)|²) dx = π ∫₀ᵗ |q|²`. For real potentials `a(t, iy) > 0` (poltoratski2024 (5.5) line 545–548 and line 503–507, printed with constant `1`; denisov2006 (194) line 3250–3255; taothiele2012 Lemma 6 line 680–683 for the discrete model). Route: `log a(t, ·)` is a primitive of `∂_z a/a` on `ℂ₊` (Tau Ceti `DifferentiableOn.hasDerivAt_wedgeIntegral_upperHalfPlane`), bounded and continuous to `ℝ` by §4.2–§4.3; §2.5 gives `log|a(t, z)| = P[log|a(t, ·)|](z)`; §2.2 gives `πy log|a(t, iy)| ↑ ∫ log|a(t, x)| dx`; the Volterra form with the approximate identity `y e^{−2yu} 1_{u>0}` (mass `1/2`) gives the limit at `i∞`.

locator.where: (5.5) line 545–548 (printed with constant 1); denisov2006 (194) line 3250–3255; taothiele2012 Lemma 6 line 680–683

tests.name: firstOrderForSmall
tests.statement: First order: for small `q`, `log|a| ≈ ½|b|²` and `∫ |∫₀ᵗ q e^{2ixs} ds|² dx = π∫₀ᵗ|q|²`, giving `π/2` again; the constant `1` printed in the sources fails this computation.

targets.name: scatteringA_eq_exp_integral_riccati
targets.statement: For `z` in the closed upper half-plane define `r(t, z) = e^{2izt} b#(t, z)/a(t, z)`. Prove that `|r(t, z)| < 1`, that `∂ₜ r = 2iz r + conj q − q r²` with `r(0, z) = 0`, that `a(t, z) = exp(∫₀ᵗ q(s) r(s, z) ds)`, that `|r(t, z)| ≤ 2∫₀ᵗ e^{−2 Im z (t − s)} |q(s)| ds`, and that `ρ(t, z) = ∫₀ᵗ q(s) e^{2izs} a(s, z)^{−2} ds`. Route: with `β = e^{2izt} b#`, the pair `(a, β)` solves `a′ = qβ`, `β′ = 2izβ + conj q a`, so `∂ₜ(|a|² − |β|²) = 4 Im z |β|² ≥ 0`; `∂ₜ ρ = q e^{2izt}/a²` follows from `det G = 1` (denisov2006 (195) line 3256–3290 for the Krein-system analogue).

tests.name: freeCase
tests.statement: Free case: `r = 0`, `a = 1`, `ρ = 0`.

tests.name: forTheSmoothComplex
tests.statement: For the smooth complex potential of §3.1, `ρ(1.7, 0.6 + 0.25i) ≈ 0.10010 + 0.21808i` both from `b/a` and from the integral formula.

tests.statement: Real `f` at `z = 0`: `r = tanh F`, `a = exp∫ f tanh F = cosh F`.

layers.title: The square-integrable scattering limit and the non-linear Fourier transform

targets.name: tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_scatteringA
targets.statement: Prove that for `z ∈ ℂ₊` with `y = Im z`: `log|a(t, z)| ≤ ‖q‖²/y` and `|ρ(t, z) − ρ(t′, z)| ≤ ‖q‖_{L²(t, ∞)} e^{−2yt}/(2√y)` for `t ≤ t′`; that `a(t, ·)`, `b(t, ·)` and `ρ(t, ·)` converge, as `t → ∞`, uniformly on every half-plane `{Im z ≥ y₀}`, `y₀ > 0`, to holomorphic limits `a(∞, ·)`, `b(∞, ·)`, `ρ(∞, ·) = b(∞, ·)/a(∞, ·)`; that `a(∞, z) = exp(∫₀^∞ q(s) r(s, z) ds)`, `ρ(∞, z) = ∫₀^∞ q(s) e^{2izs} a(s, z)^{−2} ds`, `|a(∞, z)|² − |b(∞, z)|² ≥ 1` and `|ρ(∞, z)| < 1` on `ℂ₊`; that `y log a(∞, iy) → ½‖q‖²` as `y → ∞`; and that for real potentials `a(∞, iy) ≥ 1` (denisov2006 Theorem 11.1 line 3246–3255 for Krein systems and §13 (245)–(248) line 4219–4258 for the dictionary; poltoratski2024 line 518–529). Route: §4.5 gives `|r(t, z)| ≤ 2(e^{−2y·} * |q|)(t)`, so `‖r(·, z)‖_{L²} ≤ ‖q‖/y` by Young's inequality for the kernel `e^{−2ys} 1_{s ≥ 0}` of `L¹` norm `1/(2y)`, and `|log a(t, z)| ≤ ∫|q||r| ≤ ‖q‖²/y`; the tails of `∫ q r` and of `∫ q e^{2izs} a^{−2}` are bounded by Cauchy–Schwarz.

tests.name: theLimitsAgreeWith
tests.statement: `q ∈ L¹ ∩ L²`: the limits agree with the uniform limits of §4.2 on the closed half-plane.

tests.name: theBoundDegeneratesAs
tests.statement: The bound degenerates as `y → 0`: for `q = 1_{[0,T]}`, `log|a(T, x)|` at `x = 0` is `log cosh T`, which is unbounded in `T` although `log|a(T, iy)| ≤ T/y` holds for each `y > 0`.

targets.name: nlft
targets.statement: Define the non-linear Fourier transform of `q` as `q⌃ = ρ(∞, ·)`, a holomorphic function on `ℂ₊` with `|q⌃| < 1`, together with its boundary function `q⌃*` on `ℝ` given by §2.5 (poltoratski2024 line 550–560; mauth2022 line 190–201). Its API:

api.name: truncationsOnItExtends
api.statement: Truncations: `(q_T)⌃ = ρ(T, ·)` on `ℂ₊`; it extends continuously to the closed half-plane and its boundary function is `x ↦ b(T, x)/a(T, x)` (poltoratski2024 line 556–560).

api.name: forIntegrableOnIs
api.statement: For `q` integrable on `[0, ∞)`, `q⌃` is continuous on the closed half-plane, `q⌃* = lim ρ(T, ·)` uniformly on `ℝ`, and `q⌃*(x) → 0` as `|x| → ∞`.

tests.name: withConstantExplicitlyWith
tests.statement: `q = c 1_{[0, T]}` with `c` constant: `q⌃*(x) = b(T, x)/a(T, x)` explicitly, with `|q⌃*(x)|² = |c|² sin²(κT)/(κ² + |c|² sin²(κT))`, `κ = √(x² − |c|²)`; at `x = 0`, `q⌃*(0) = (c/|c|) tanh(|c|T)`.

tests.name: isStrictOnThe
tests.statement: `|q⌃| < 1` is strict on `ℂ₊`: the boundary function of `ρ(T, ·)` for `q = 1_{[0,1]}` has supremum `tanh 1 ≈ 0.762`, attained at `x = 0`.

targets.name: normSq_scatteringA_infty_sub_normSq_scatteringB_infty_ae
targets.statement: Prove that `a(∞, ·)` has nontangential boundary values `a(∞, x) ≠ 0` and `b(∞, ·)` has boundary values `b(∞, x) = q⌃*(x) a(∞, x)` at almost every `x`; the non-linear Plancherel inequality `∫_ℝ log|a(∞, x)| dx ≤ (π/2)‖q‖²`; that for every `T ≥ 0`, with `(a₁, b₁, ρ₁)` the data of `q` at time `T`, `ρ₂ = (q_{>T})⌃*` and `u(x) = e^{2ixT} conj(a₁(x))/a₁(x)`, one has for almost every `x` `q⌃*(x) = (u ρ₂ + ρ₁)/(1 + u ρ₂ conj ρ₁)`, `a(∞, x) = a₂(x) a₁(x)(1 + u ρ₂ conj ρ₁)` and `|a(∞, x)|² − |b(∞, x)|² = |a₂(x)|² − |b₂(x)|²`, where `(a₂, b₂)` are the boundary values of the limits for `q_{>T}`; and that `|a(∞, x)|² − |b(∞, x)|² = 1` almost everywhere, so `−log(1 − |q⌃*(x)|²) = 2 log|a(∞, x)|` (poltoratski2024 line 518–548, 569–577). Route: `1/a(∞, ·)` is bounded by `1` and not zero, so by §2.5 its boundary values exist and are nonzero almost everywhere. Plancherel inequality: `log|a(∞, ·)| ≥ 0` is harmonic, so §2.2 gives `c Im z + P[ν]`, and `πy log|a(∞, iy)| → (π/2)‖q‖²` (§5.1) forces `c = 0` and `ν(ℝ) = (π/2)‖q‖²`, while §2.4 identifies the absolutely continuous part `ν_ac = log|a(∞, x)| dx`. The concatenation law of §4.1 passes to the limit in `ℂ₊` and then to the boundary. For the identity, `δ = |a(∞)|² − |b(∞)|² − 1 ≥ 0` equals the corresponding quantity of the tail, which satisfies `log(1 + δ) ≤ 2 log|a₂|`; integrate and apply the Plancherel inequality to the tail, whose right side is `π‖q‖²_{L²(T,∞)} → 0`.

targets.name: deBrangesSpace_diracE_eq_paleyWiener
targets.statement: Let `t > 0`. Prove that `B(E(t, ·)) = PW_t` and `B(Ẽ(t, ·)) = PW_t` as sets, with `e^{−∫₀ᵗ|q|} ‖F‖_{L²} ≤ ‖F‖_{B(E(t,·))} ≤ e^{∫₀ᵗ|q|} ‖F‖_{L²}`, and that the reproducing kernels are `K_t(w, z) = (1/π) ∫₀ᵗ Θ(s, w)* Θ(s, z) ds` and `K̃_t(w, z) = (1/π) ∫₀ᵗ Φ(s, w)* Φ(s, z) ds` (poltoratski2024 line 269–285; mauth2022 Lemma 18 line 659–691; romanov2014 Theorem 5 (16) line 812). targets.name: weylFunction
targets.statement: For `z ∈ ℂ₊` and `t ≥ 0` define the Weyl disc `D_t(z) = {w ∈ ℂ : Im z ∫₀ᵗ |Φ(s, z) + wΘ(s, z)|² ds ≤ Im w}` and the Weyl function `m(z)` as the point of `⋂_t D_t(z)` (romanov2014 §8 Theorem 15 line 2217–2261, Lemma 23 line 2370; remling2018, Ch. 2, waived). Its API:

api.name: forIsAClosed
api.statement: For `t > 0`, `D_t(z)` is a closed disc of radius `1/(2 Im z ∫₀ᵗ |Θ(s, z)|² ds)`, decreasing in `t`. Writing `(u, v) = Φ(t, z) + wΘ(t, z)`, its boundary circle consists of the `w` with `u/v ∈ ℝ ∪ {∞}`, among them `−D(t, z)/C(t, z)` and `−B(t, z)/A(t, z)` (`A(t, z)` and `C(t, z)` do not vanish, since `Im(conj A(t, z) · C(t, z)) = Im z ∫₀ᵗ |Θ(s, z)|² ds > 0`), while `−Ẽ(t, z)/E(t, z)`, the point where `u − iv` vanishes, lies in its interior. Equivalently, `D_t(z) = {w : |Ẽ(t, z) + wE(t, z)| ≤ |Ẽ#(t, z) + wE#(t, z)|}`.

api.name: limitPointForSo
api.statement: Limit point: `∫₀^∞ |Θ(s, z)|² ds = ∞` for `z ∈ ℂ₊`, so the intersection is a single point.

api.name: isTheUniqueWith
api.statement: `m(z)` is the unique `w` with `Φ(·, z) + wΘ(·, z) ∈ L²(ℝ₊; ℂ²)`.

api.name: isHolomorphicOnWith
api.statement: `m` is holomorphic on `ℂ₊` with `Im m > 0`, and `−Ẽ(t, ·)/E(t, ·) → m` locally uniformly on `ℂ₊`, with error at most twice the radius.

api.name: theDirichletWeylFunction
api.statement: The Dirichlet Weyl function is `−1/m = lim E(t, ·)/Ẽ(t, ·)`.

api.name: routeOfAtTime
api.statement: Route: `Im(conj u · v)` of `Φ + wΘ` at time `t` is `−Im w + Im z ∫₀ᵗ|Φ + wΘ|²` by the Christoffel–Darboux identity; nesting is monotonicity in `t`; since `A, B, C, D` are real entire (§3.1), `(u − iv)(t) = Ẽ(t, z) + wE(t, z)` and `(u + iv)(t) = Ẽ#(t, z) + wE#(t, z)`, and `Im(conj u · v) = (|u − iv|² − |u + iv|²)/4` gives the second description, a disc because `|E(t, z)| > |E#(t, z)|` (§3.3); `u − iv` vanishes at `w = −Ẽ/E`, where `u + iv ≠ 0` because `(u, v) ≠ 0`, so that point lies inside the disc. Limit point: if `Θ(·, z₀) ∈ L²` for some `z₀ ∈ ℂ₊`, every solution is square-integrable at `z₀` and then, by variation of constants and §1.1, at every `z`; at `z = 0`, `det[Θ, Φ] = 1` gives `1 ≤ |Θ||Φ|`, which is not integrable on `[0, ∞)`.

For the smooth complex potential of §3.1 at the same `t` and `z`, `w₀ = −Ẽ/E ≈ 0.3468 + 0.7493i` has `Im z ∫₀ᵗ |Φ + w₀Θ|² ≈ 0.4541 < Im w₀`, and the disc `|Ẽ + wE| ≤ |Ẽ# + wE#|` has radius `≈ 0.6538`, equal to the stated radius, with `−D/C` and `−B/A` on its circle. api.statement: Variational formula: `S(σ | ν) = inf {∫ F dν − ∫ (1 + log F) dσ : F continuous, min F > 0}` (Theorem 5.2 line 1864).

api.name: jointWeakUpperSemicontinuity
api.statement: Joint weak upper semicontinuity: `σₙ → σ` and `νₙ → ν` weakly imply `S(σ | ν) ≥ lim sup S(σₙ | νₙ)` (Corollary 5.3 line 1960).

api.name: transportToTheLine
api.statement: Transport to the line: for a Poisson-finite `μ = w dx + μ_s` on `ℝ`, with `σ` the Cayley image of `Π/π` and `ν` the Cayley image of `μ/(π(1 + x²))` together with any atom at `1`, `S(σ | ν) = (1/π) ∫ log w dΠ`.

tests.name: aPointMass
tests.statement: Let `σ = dθ/2π` be the Cayley image of `Π/π`: the `σ` of the transport bullet, a non-atomic probability measure. Then `ν = σ` gives `S = 0`, and `ν = 2σ` gives `S = log 2 = log ν(X)`. For the point mass `ν = δ₁`, the set `X ∖ {1}` has `ν`-measure `0` and `σ`-measure `1`. So `σ` is not absolutely continuous with respect to `ν`, and `S = −∞`. Two equal point masses, by contrast, give `S(δ₁ | δ₁) = 0`, so this case needs a non-atomic first argument.

tests.name: semicontinuityIsNotContinuity
tests.statement: Semicontinuity is not continuity: `νₙ = (1 + sin nθ) dθ/2π → σ` weakly while `S(σ | νₙ) = (1/2π)∫₀^{2π} log(1 + sin θ) dθ = −log 2 < 0 = S(σ | σ)`.

tests.name: freeSpectralMeasure
tests.statement: Free spectral measure `μ = dx`: `S(σ | ν) = (1/π)∫ log 1 dΠ = 0`.

targets.name: integrable_log_spectralDensity
targets.statement: Let `q` be square-integrable. Prove that `∫ log w dΠ ≥ −2π log 2 − π‖q‖²` and the same for `w̃`; hence `log w, log w̃ ∈ L¹(Π)` and `w, w̃ > 0` almost everywhere (poltoratski2024 line 263–268; mauth2022 Theorem 3 line 702–707; denisov2006 Theorem 11.1 line 3246 with the dictionary of §13). Route: for the truncation `q_T`, `w_T = |E(T, ·)|^{−2}` and `|E(T, x)| = |a(T, x) + b(T, x)| ≤ 2|a(T, x)|`, so `∫ log w_T dΠ ≥ −2π log 2 − 2∫ log|a(T, x)| dx = −2π log 2 − π‖q‖²_{L²(0,T)}` by §4.4; the measures converge as in §6.6, and §6.7 transfers the bound to `μ`; `log⁺ w ≤ w` is `Π`-integrable because `μ` is Poisson-finite.

tests.name: freeCaseAnd
tests.statement: Free case: `w = 1` and `0 ≥ −2π log 2`.

tests.name: realConstantOnAt
tests.statement: Real constant `f = c` on `[0, T]`: at `x = 0`, `log w(0) = −2cT`, and `|E(T, 0)| = e^{cT} ≤ 2|a(T, 0)| = 2 cosh cT`.

tests.name: squareIntegrabilityIsNeeded
tests.statement: Square-integrability is needed: `f ≡ c > 0` on `[0, ∞)` gives `w = 0` on `(−c, c)` and `∫ log w dΠ = −∞`.

targets.name: IsMeromorphicInner
targets.statement: Call a bounded holomorphic `θ` on `ℂ₊` inner when `|θ*| = 1` almost everywhere (§2.5), and meromorphic inner when it moreover extends to a meromorphic function on `ℂ`; for `λ ∈ ℂ₊` the Blaschke factor is `b_λ(z) = (z − λ)/(z − conj λ)` (poltoratski2024 line 307–331; mauth2022 line 446–453). Its API, for `E` Hermite–Biehler, entire of order at most one, with no real zeros:
hypotheses: E Hermite–Biehler, entire of order at most one, no real zeros (for the phase theorem)

api.name: isMeromorphicInnerAnd
api.statement: `θ_E = E#/E` is meromorphic inner, and products of meromorphic inner functions are meromorphic inner.

api.name: writingWithContinuousOn
api.statement: Writing `E(x) = |E(x)| e^{−iψ(x)}` with `ψ` continuous on `ℝ`, so that `ψ = −arg E` (for `E = E(t, ·)` one may take `ψ = −φ(t, ·)`, the negative of the branch `φ` of §3.2), `θ_E(x) = e^{2iψ(x)}` and `ψ′(x) = π K(x, x)/|E(x)|² > 0`, with `K` the kernel of §6.1.

api.name: ifAreTheZeros
api.statement: If `(ζₙ)` are the zeros of `θ_E` in `ℂ₊` with multiplicity (the conjugates of the zeros of `E`), then `Σ Im ζₙ/(1 + |ζₙ|²) < ∞` and there is `c ≥ 0` with `2ψ′(x) = |θ_E′(x)| = c + Σₙ 2 Im ζₙ/|x − ζₙ|²` for every `x ∈ ℝ` (poltoratski2024 line 312–321 and the proof of Lemma 1, line 337–346).

api.name: routeHadamardFactorisationOf
api.statement: Route: Hadamard factorisation of `E` with genus one (AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §0.23) gives `E′/E = β + Σₙ (1/(z − zₙ) + 1/zₙ)`; on `ℝ`, `θ_E′/θ_E = −2i Im(E′/E)`; the Hermite–Biehler inequality `|θ_E| ≤ 1` on `ℂ₊`, evaluated along `iy`, forces the Blaschke condition and `c ≥ 0`.

tests.name: noZerosAnd
tests.statement: `E = e^{−itz}`: `θ_E = e^{2itz}`, no zeros, `|θ_E′| = 2t = c`, and `ψ(x) = tx`, `ψ′ = t = π(t/π)/1`, while the branch of §3.2 is `φ(t, x) = −tx`, with `∂ₜφ = −x`.

tests.name: isInnerButHas
tests.statement: `e^{−i/z}` is inner but has an essential singularity at `0`, so it is not meromorphic inner; `e^{−iz}` is unbounded on `ℂ₊` (`|e^{−iz}| = e^{Im z}`), so the reflected convention `E/E#` is not inner.

targets.name: exists_zero_mem_ball_of_phaseDeriv
targets.statement: Let `θ` be meromorphic inner with the representation of §7.1, `0 < ε < 1` and `x, y ∈ ℝ` with `|θ′(x)| > (1 + ε)|θ′(y)|`. Prove that `θ` has a zero in the disc `{ζ : |ζ − x| < 3|y − x|/ε}` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 1 line 332–360; mauth2022 Lemma 29 line 1624). Route: some summand satisfies the same inequality, which places `ζₙ` inside an Apollonius circle with foci `x` and `y`.
hypotheses: θ meromorphic inner with the representation of 7.1

tests.name: andForEveryThe
tests.statement: `θ = b_i`, `x = 0`, `y = 1`: `|θ′(0)| = 2`, `|θ′(1)| = 1`, and for every `ε < 1` the disc of radius `3/ε` about `0` contains `i`.

tests.name: isConstantTheHypothesis
tests.statement: `θ = e^{2itz}`: `|θ′|` is constant, the hypothesis never holds, and `θ` has no zeros.

tests.name: ratioHypothesisFailsRatio
tests.statement: `θ = b_{10i}`, `ε = 1/2`: `|θ′(0)| = 0.2`, `|θ′(5)| = 0.16` (ratio `1.25`, hypothesis fails), `|θ′(10)| = 0.1` (ratio `2`), and the disc of radius `60` about `0` contains `10i`.

targets.name: diracInner
targets.statement: For a real potential define the Dirac inner functions `θ(t, ·) = E#(t, ·)/E(t, ·)` and `θ̃(t, ·) = Ẽ#(t, ·)/Ẽ(t, ·)`; a resonance at time `t` is a zero of `E(t, ·)`, equivalently the conjugate of a zero of `θ(t, ·)` (poltoratski2024 §4 line 361–468). Its API:

api.name: forBothAreMeromorphic
api.statement: For `t > 0` both are meromorphic inner (§3.3, §7.1); `θ(0, ·) = 1` and `θ̃(0, ·) = −1`; `|θ(t, x)| = 1` on `ℝ`.

api.name: riccatiEquationWhereverFor
api.statement: Riccati equation (4.1): `θ(t, z) = 1 + ∫₀ᵗ (2izθ + f(1 − θ²))(s, z) ds` wherever `E(s, z) ≠ 0` for `s ∈ [0, t]`, and likewise for `θ̃` with initial value `−1`.

api.name: resonanceMotionIfIs
api.statement: Resonance motion (4.3): if `ζ(t)` is a simple zero of `θ(t, ·)` on a time interval, then `ζ` is absolutely continuous with `ζ′(t) = −f(t)/∂_zθ(t, ζ(t))` almost everywhere (poltoratski2024 line 425–444).

api.name: routeFromTheZero
api.statement: Route: (4.1) from §3.2; the zero is `ζ(t) = (1/2πi)∮ w ∂_wθ(t, w)/θ(t, w) dw` over a small fixed circle, absolutely continuous in `t`.

tests.name: freeCaseSolvesWith
tests.statement: Free case: `θ = e^{2itz}` solves `∂ₜθ = 2izθ`, with no zeros.

tests.name: constantAtIsReal
tests.statement: Constant `f = c` at `z = 0`: `E(t, 0) = e^{ct}` is real, so `θ(t, 0) = 1` and the right side `f(1 − 1²) = 0` is consistent; `θ̃(t, 0) = (i e^{−ct})/(−i e^{−ct}) = −1`.

tests.name: forComplexPotentialsThe
tests.statement: For complex potentials the equation reads `∂ₜθ = 2izθ + conj q − qθ²`; the real form is its `g = 0` case.

layers.title: Universality and the approximation of Hermite–Biehler functions

targets.name: resonanceTimes
targets.statement: Define, for `s ∈ ℝ` and `C > 0` (or a function `C(t) > 0`), the sets of times `T₀(s, C) = {t > 0 : E(t, ·) has a zero in Q(s, C/t)}` and `T₁(s, C) = {t > 0 : every zero of E(t, ·) in Q(s, C/t) has imaginary part < −1/t}`, and their analogues `T̃₀`, `T̃₁` for `Ẽ`; and `γ(p) = √2/√(sinh 2p)` for `p > 0` (poltoratski2024 line 846–849 and 997–1001; mauth2022 line 1245–1257).

api.name: andIncreaseAndDecrease
api.statement: `T₀(s, C)` and `T₁(s, C)` increase and decrease in `C` respectively, and `(0, ∞) ∖ T₀(s, C) ⊆ T₁(s, C)`.

api.name: asAndForReal
api.statement: `γ(p)² sinh 2p = 2`, `γ(p) ~ 2e^{−p}` as `p → ∞`, and for real `a`, `|γ(p) sin(a + ip)|² = 2(sin²a + sinh²p)/sinh 2p` lies in `[tanh p, coth p]` and tends to `1` as `p → ∞`, uniformly in `a`.

tests.name: freeCaseHasNo
tests.statement: Free case: `E(t, ·) = e^{−itz}` has no zeros, so `T₀(s, C) = ∅` and `T₁(s, C) = (0, ∞)`.

tests.name: andForRealWhich
tests.statement: `γ(1) = √2/√(sinh 2) ≈ 1.41421/1.90443 ≈ 0.7426`; and for real `a`, `|γ(p) sin(a + ip)|² = 2(sin²a + sinh²p)/sinh 2p`, which tends to `1` as `p → ∞` uniformly in `a`.

tests.name: aZeroAtPuts
tests.statement: A zero at `s − i/(2t)` puts `t` in `T₀(s, 1)` and outside `T₁(s, 1)`; a zero at `s − 2i/t` puts `t` in `T₀(s, 3) ∩ T₁(s, 3)`.

targets.name: tendsto_spectralDensity_mul_kernel_div_sinc
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s ∈ ℝ` and every `C > 0`, `sup_{λ ∈ Q(s, C/t)} |w(s) K_t(λ, λ)/Sinc_t(λ, λ) − 1| → 0` as `t → ∞`, where `K_t(λ, λ) = sup{|F(λ)|² : F ∈ PW_t, ∫|F|² dμ ≤ 1}` and `Sinc_t(λ, λ) = sup{|F(λ)|² : F ∈ PW_t, ∫|F|² dx ≤ 1} = sinh(2t Im λ)/(2π Im λ)` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 2 line 630–727; mauth2022 Lemma 21 line 794). Route (upper bound): let `G = O_{(1/2) log w}` be the outer function with `|G|² = w` on `ℝ` (§2.8; `log w ∈ L¹(Π)` by §6.8). Take `s` with `w(s) > 0` that is a Lebesgue point of `√(M_1 P[|log w|])` (§2.3) and at which `G` has a nontangential limit, and multiply `G` by a unimodular constant so that this limit is `√w(s)`. Almost every `s` qualifies: the limits exist almost everywhere by the boundary-value bullet of §2.8, because `w dx ≤ μ` is Poisson-finite. Rescale by `t`: `G_t(z) = G(s + z/t)` is outer with boundary modulus `√w(s + ·/t)`, by the covariance of §2.1 and the characterisation of §2.8. A counterexample sequence `fₙ ∈ PW_1` with `∫ |fₙ|² w(s + ·/kₙ) dx ≤ 1` has `e^{iz}fₙ ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` (§2.7). So `e^{iz}fₙ G_{kₙ} ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` with norm at most `1`, by the outer-multiplier bullet of §2.8. A subsequence converges weakly and normally (§2.6), and §2.7's characterisation produces an `H ∈ PW_1` violating the extremal value. Lower bound: `|Sinc(t, λ, ·)|²/‖Sinc(t, λ, ·)‖²₂` is an approximate identity at `s`, so its `μ`-integral tends to `w(s)` at almost every `s` (§2.4), and `Sinc(t, λ, ·)/‖·‖_μ` is a competitor.

tests.name: freeCaseAndThe
tests.statement: Free case: `μ = dx`, `w ≡ 1`, `K = Sinc`, and the ratio is `1` for every `t`.

tests.name: forRealSoThe
tests.statement: For real `λ`, `Sinc_t(λ, λ) = t/π`, so the statement says `K_t(λ, λ) = (t/π)(1/w(s) + o(1))` uniformly for `|λ − s| ≤ C/t`.

tests.name: theStatementFailsAt
tests.statement: The statement fails at points with `w(s) = 0`: for `f ≡ c` (not square-integrable) and `s ∈ (−c, c)`, `w(s) = 0` while `K_t(s, s) > 0`.

targets.name: kernel_sub_sinc_L2_isLittleO
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s` and every `C > 0`, `sup_{λ ∈ Q(s, C/t)} ‖K_t(λ, ·) − Sinc_t(λ, ·)/w(s)‖²_{L²(μ)} = o(t)` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 3 line 729–751; mauth2022 Corollary 3 line 1104). Route: expand the square using the reproducing property and the approximate-identity limit of §8.2, then use §8.2 and `Sinc_t(λ, λ) ≍ t`.

tests.name: freeCaseTheLeft
tests.statement: Free case: the left side is `0`.

tests.name: scalingForRealSo
tests.statement: Scaling: `Sinc_t(λ, λ) = t/π` for real `λ`, so `o(t)` is `o(Sinc_t(λ, λ))`, the natural scale.

tests.name: theNormalisationIsForced
tests.statement: The normalisation `Sinc/w(s)` is forced: with `Sinc/√w(s)` the same expansion gives `‖K_t(λ, ·) − Sinc_t(λ, ·)/√w(s)‖²_μ = Sinc_t(λ, λ)(1/√w(s) − 1)² + o(t)`, of order `t` unless `w(s) = 1`.

targets.name: kernel_sub_sinc_isLittleO
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s` and every `C > 0`, `sup_{λ, z ∈ Q(s, C/t)} |K(t, λ, z) − Sinc(t, λ, z)/w(s)| = o(t)` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 4 (6.6) line 756–792; mauth2022 Lemma 22 line 1129). Route: `Δ = K(t, λ_t, ·) − Sinc(t, λ_t, ·)/w(s)` lies in `PW_t` (§6.2, §2.7), so `e^{itz}Δ ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` (§2.7). Since `w dx ≤ μ`, §8.3 gives `∫ |Δ|² w dx ≤ ∫ |Δ|² dμ = o(t)`. Let `G = O_{(1/2) log w}` be the outer function with `|G|² = w` on `ℝ` (§2.8, §6.8). The outer-multiplier bullet of §2.8 then gives `F(t, ·) = e^{itz} G Δ ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` with `‖F(t, ·)‖² = ∫ |Δ|² w dx = o(t)`. Hence `F(t, ·)` has nontangential maximal function `o(√t)` in `L²` (§2.6); choose two real points on either side of `Q(s, C/t)` where it is `o(t)` and where `√(M_1 P[log w])` is controlled; the difference of kernels is real entire, so the bound on the boundary of a rhombus symmetric about `ℝ` gives the bound inside by the maximum principle.

tests.name: freeCaseTheDifference
tests.statement: Free case: the difference is `0`.

tests.name: onTheDiagonalConsistent
tests.statement: On the diagonal `z = λ = s`: `K(t, s, s) − (t/π)/w(s) = o(t)`, consistent with §8.2.

tests.name: theDifferenceIsReal
tests.statement: The difference is real entire for real `λ` because `A`, `C` are real entire (§3.1); for a complex `λ` the same holds for `K(t, λ, ·) − Sinc(t, λ, ·)/w(s)` and its reflection.

targets.name: kernelNumerator_sub_sin_tendsto
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s` and every `C > 0`, `sup_{λ, z ∈ Q(s, C/t)} |D(t, λ, z) − sin(t(λ − z))/w(s)| → 0`, and that there is `C(t) → ∞` with the same conclusion over `Q(s, C(t)/t)` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 5 (7.2) and Corollary 1 (7.3), line 814–842; mauth2022 Corollaries 4–5 line 1205–1242). Route: multiply §8.4 by `π|λ − z| ≤ 2√2 πC/t`; a diagonal argument over `C = 1, 2, …` gives `C(t)`.

locator.where: Lemma 5 (7.2), Corollary 1 (7.3), line 814–842; mauth2022 Corollaries 4–5 line 1205–1242

tests.statement: Free case: `D = cos tz sin tλ − sin tz cos tλ = sin(t(λ − z))`, exactly.

targets.name: diracE_approx_sin_near_resonance
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s` and every `D > 1` with `T₀(s, D)` unbounded there is `C(t) > D`, `C(t) → ∞`, such that: if `z(t) = x(t) − iy(t)` is a continuous choice of zeros of `E(t, ·)` in `Q(s, C(t)/t)` for `t ∈ T₀(s, C)`, then there is a continuous unimodular `α(s, t)` with `sup_{z ∈ Q(s, C(t)/t)} |E(t, z) − α(s, t) γ(t y(t)) sin(t(z − z(t)))/√w(s)| → 0` as `t → ∞` in `T₀(s, C) ∩ {t y(t) > 1}`, and with error `o(γ(t y(t)))` without the restriction `t y(t) > 1`; and, equivalently for the Dirac inner function on `Q₊(s, C(t)/t) = Q(s, C(t)/t) ∩ ℂ₊`, `sup |θ(t, z) − conj(α)² sin(t(z − conj z(t)))/sin(t(z − z(t)))| → 0`, with the derivative relation at the zero `conj z(t)` of `θ(t, ·)`: `α² ∂_zθ(t, conj z(t)) = (1 + o(1)) t/sin(2it y(t))` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 6 and Corollary 2, line 850–917, Remark 3 line 863; mauth2022 Lemma 23 line 1258 and Lemma 32 line 1765). Route: `E(t, z(t)) = 0` gives `A(t, z(t)) = iC(t, z(t)) = β`, so `D(t, z(t), ·) = iβE(t, ·)`, and §8.5 makes `iβE` close to `sin(t(· − z(t)))/w(s)`; the determinant identity (2.2) at two points fixes `2|β|²w(s) = (1 + o(1)) sinh(2t y(t))`.
hypotheses: a.e. s with T₀(s,D) unbounded for some D > 1

locator.where: Lemma 6, Corollary 2, Remark 3, line 850–917; mauth2022 Lemma 23 line 1258, Lemma 32 line 1765

tests.name: theNormalisationWithReal
tests.statement: The normalisation: `|γ(p) sin(t(x − z(t)))|` with `t(x − x(t)) = a` real equals `(2(sin²a + sinh²p)/sinh 2p)^{1/2}` with `p = t y(t)`, between `γ(p) sinh p` and `γ(p) cosh p`, and tends to `1` as `p → ∞`, matching `|E(t, x)| ≈ 1/√w(s)` away from resonances.

tests.statement: Determinant consistency: with `E ≈ αγ(p) sin(t(z − z₀))/√w` and `Ẽ ≈ αγ(p) cos(t(z − z̃₀))/√w̃`, the quantity `E Ẽ# − Ẽ E#` equals `2i` exactly when `cos(t(x̃₀ − x₀)) = √(w w̃)` (computed in §9.2).

tests.statement: Free case: `T₀ = ∅` and the statement is vacuous.

targets.name: diracE_approx_exp_away_from_resonance
targets.statement: Prove (poltoratski2024 Corollary 3 line 1002–1012 and the argument of line 918–996; mauth2022 Corollary 6 line 1397–1408): (1) for almost every `s` there are `C(t) → ∞` and `z(t) = x(t) − iy(t) ∈ ℂ₋` with `sup_{z ∈ Q(s, C(t)/t)} |E(t, z) − α(s, t) γ(t y(t)) sin(t(z − z(t)))/√w(s)| → 0` as `t → ∞` in `T₁(s, C)`, `|α| = 1`, where `z(t)` is a zero of `E(t, ·)` when `t ∈ T₀(s, C)`; (2) if this holds and `t ∉ T₀(s, C(t))` for all large `t`, then for every `D > 0`, `sup_{z ∈ Q(s, D/t)} |E(t, z) + iα(s, t) e^{−itz}/√w(s)| → 0`. Route: §8.5 with two values of the second argument shows that `(A(t, x), C(t, x))` has modulus bounded below and rotates on `ℝ ∩ Q(s, C/t)`; choosing its zero crossings gives `E ≈ −cos(t(z − x₂))/(c₂w) − i sin(t(z − x₀))/(c₁w)`; if `t(x₂ − x₀)` were not `o(1)` modulo `2π`, or `c₁ − c₂` not `o(1)`, the phase derivative of `E` would vary by a factor `1 + ε` on an interval of length `8π/t`, and §7.2 would give a zero in `Q(s, C/t)`.

tests.name: freeCaseAndSo
tests.statement: Free case: `E = e^{−itz}` and `w = 1`, so (2) holds exactly with `α = i`: `e^{−itz} + i·i·e^{−itz} = 0`.

tests.name: withAndAndOn
tests.statement: With `A = t(z − x)` and `p = t y`, `γ(p) sin(A + ip) = i e^{−iA}(1 + O(e^{2|Im A| − 2p}))`, and `|Im A| ≤ D` on `Q(s, D/t)`; so (1) passes into (2), with `α` replaced by a unimodular multiple, when `t y(t) → ∞`.

tests.name: atAPointWith
tests.statement: At a point `s` with `w(s) = 0` the normalisation `1/√w(s)` is undefined; for square-integrable `f` such points form a null set (§6.8), which is why the statement holds almost everywhere and not everywhere.

targets.name: diracE_diracETilde_joint_approx
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s` there is `C(t) → ∞` such that for every `t ∈ T₁(s, C) ∩ T̃₁(s, C)` there are `z(t) = u(t) − ip(t)`, `z̃(t) = ũ(t) − ip(t)` with `p(t) > 0` and a unimodular `α(t)` with `sup_{Q(s, C(t)/t)} |E(t, z) − α γ(tp) sin(t(z − z(t)))/√w(s)| → 0`, `sup_{Q(s, C(t)/t)} |Ẽ(t, z) − α γ(tp) cos(t(z − z̃(t)))/√w̃(s)| → 0`, `p(t) > C(t)/t` for `t ∉ T₀(s, C)`, `p(t) ≤ C(t)/t` for `t ∈ T₀(s, C)`, and `cos(t(ũ(t) − u(t))) = √(w(s) w̃(s))` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 7 line 1028–1097, (8.1); mauth2022 Lemma 43 line 3140). Route: §8.7 for `E` and `Ẽ`; inserting the two approximants into the determinant identity (2.2) on `ℝ ∩ Q(s, D/t)` forces equal imaginary parts and the cosine relation. The relation needs `√(w w̃) ≤ 1`, which is §6.5.

tests.name: soAnAngleWith
tests.statement: `√(w w̃) ≤ 1` (§6.5), so an angle with the required cosine exists; at the point `x = 0` of the compactly supported example of §6.5, `w w̃ = 1` and `ũ − u ∈ (2π/t)ℤ`.

tests.name: theExactComputationOf
tests.statement: The exact computation of §9.2 shows that the two approximants satisfy `EẼ# − ẼE# = 2i` identically in `z ∈ ℝ` under the cosine relation (numerically `2i` for `w = 0.7`, `w̃ = 0.9`).

tests.name: theRelationIsForced
tests.statement: The relation is forced: for the two approximants with `t(ũ − u) = Φ`, the determinant on `ℝ` is `γ(p)² cos Φ sin(2ip)/√(w w̃) = 2i cos Φ/√(w w̃)`; with `ũ = u` and `w w̃ = 0.63` it is `≈ 2.52i ≠ 2i`.

targets.name: diracE_exact_form_at_point
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s` and every `C > 1` there are `ε₀ > 0` and `D = D(C, s)` such that if for some `t > 0` the two approximations of §8.8 hold on `Q(s, 3C/t)` with error `ε < ε₀`, with parameters `x, x̃, y` satisfying `1 < ty < 2C`, `−π/2 < t(x̃ − x) < π/2` and `cos(t(x̃ − x)) = √(w(s) w̃(s))`, then there are `x′, x̃′, y′` and a unimodular `α′` with `|tx′ − tx| + |tx̃′ − tx̃| + |ty′ − ty| + |α′ − α| < Dε`, `x̃′ − x′ = x̃ − x`, and exactly `E(t, s) = α′ γ(ty) sin(t(s − (x′ − iy′)))/√w(s)` and `Ẽ(t, s) = α′ γ(ty) cos(t(s − (x̃′ − iy′)))/√w̃(s)` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 8 line 1116–1172; mauth2022 Lemma 45 line 3251). Route: the quotient `sin(t(z − (x − iy)))/cos(t(z − (x̃ − iy)))` has derivative bounded below near `s`, so it attains the value `E(t, s)/Ẽ(t, s)` at a point `a` with `|a − s| ≤ D₂ε/t`; translate the parameters by `a − s` and use (2.2) for the moduli.
hypotheses: the approximations of 8.8 on Q(s,3C/t) with error ε < ε₀

tests.name: ifTheApproximationsAre
tests.statement: If the approximations are exact at `s`, the conclusion holds with `x′ = x`, `x̃′ = x̃`, `y′ = y`, `α′ = α`.

tests.name: theConstraintKeepsThe
tests.statement: The constraint `1 < ty < 2C` keeps the quotient holomorphic near `s` (no zero of the cosine within `1/(2t)` of `ℝ ∩ Q(s, 3C/t)`).

tests.name: moduliTheExactForms
tests.statement: Moduli: the exact forms give `|E(t, s)|²/|Ẽ(t, s)|² = (w̃/w)|sin|²/|cos|²`, and (2.2) at the real point `s` fixes the common factor `γ(ty)` once the cosine relation holds.

layers.title: Pointwise convergence of the non-linear Fourier transform

targets.name: intervalScattering
targets.statement: For `0 ≤ t₁ ≤ t₂` define the transfer matrix `M_{t₁→t₂} = M(t₂, ·) M(t₁, ·)^{−1}` and its Hermite–Biehler and scattering functions `E_{t₁→t₂}`, `Ẽ_{t₁→t₂}`, `a_{t₁→t₂}`, `b_{t₁→t₂}` as those of the potential `f(t₁ + ·) 1_{[0, t₂ − t₁]}` at time `t₂ − t₁` (poltoratski2024 line 1183–1210). Its API:

api.name: isTheFundamentalMatrix
api.statement: `M_{t₁→t₂}` is the fundamental matrix of `f(t₁ + ·)` at time `t₂ − t₁` (§3.1 chain rule).

api.name: andPoltoratskiLine
api.statement: `a_{t₁→t₂} = e^{i(t₂−t₁)z}(E(t₂)Ẽ#(t₁) − Ẽ(t₂)E#(t₁))/(2i)` and `b_{t₁→t₂} = e^{i(t₂−t₁)z}(Ẽ(t₂)E(t₁) − E(t₂)Ẽ(t₁))/(2i)` (poltoratski2024 (9.1)–(9.3) line 1228–1319).

api.name: poltoratskiLine
api.statement: `∫ log|a_{t₁→t₂}(x)| dx = (π/2) ∫_{t₁}^{t₂} f²` (§4.4; poltoratski2024 line 1209–1210).

api.name: theNonLinearFourier
api.statement: The non-linear Fourier transform of `f 1_{(t₁, t₂)}` is `e^{2izt₁} b_{t₁→t₂}/a_{t₁→t₂}` (§5.6 translation).

tests.name: andTheFormulasReduce
tests.statement: `t₁ = 0`: `E(0) = 1`, `Ẽ(0) = −i`, and the formulas reduce to `a = e^{it₂z}(E + iẼ)/2`, `b = e^{it₂z}(E − iẼ)/2`.

tests.name: freeCase
tests.statement: Free case: `a_{t₁→t₂} = 1`, `b_{t₁→t₂} = 0`.

targets.name: intervalScattering_trig_eval
targets.statement: Let `s ∈ ℝ`, `w, w̃ > 0` with `w w̃ ≤ 1`, `Φ ∈ (−π/2, π/2)` with `cos Φ = √(w w̃)`, and for `k = 1, 2` let `t_k > 0`, `x_k ∈ ℝ`, `y_k > 0`, `|α_k| = 1` with `E(t_k, s) = α_k γ(t_k y_k) sin θ_k/√w` and `Ẽ(t_k, s) = α_k γ(t_k y_k) cos(θ_k − Φ)/√w̃`, where `θ_k = t_k(s − x_k + iy_k)`. Put `υ = t₁y₁`, `e = ε₁ + iε₂` with `ε₁ = t₂(s − x₂) − t₁(s − x₁)`, `ε₂ = t₂y₂ − t₁y₁`, and `N = (sinh 2υ sinh 2(υ + ε₂))^{1/2}`. Prove the exact identities `a_{t₁→t₂}(s) = e^{i(t₂−t₁)s} α₂ conj(α₁) sin(e + 2iυ)/(iN)`, `b_{t₁→t₂}(s) = −e^{i(t₂−t₁)s} α₂ α₁ sin(e)/(iN)`, and hence `(f 1_{(t₁,t₂)})⌃(s) = −e^{2ist₁} α₁² sin e/sin(e + 2iυ)` (poltoratski2024 (9.2), (9.4) and line 1253–1347). Route: `sin A cos(B − Φ) − cos(A − Φ) sin B = cos Φ sin(A − B)` with `A = θ₂`, `B = conj θ₁` (and the analogous identity for `b`), and `γ(p)γ(p′) = 2/(sinh 2p sinh 2p′)^{1/2}`.
hypotheses: E(t_k,s), Ẽ(t_k,s) of the stated sin/cos forms, k = 1, 2

tests.name: asSuRequiresOn
tests.statement: `|a|² − |b|² = (sinh²(ε₂ + 2υ) − sinh² ε₂)/N² = 1`, as SU(1,1) requires on `ℝ`; numerically, for `w = 0.7`, `w̃ = 0.9`, `s = 0.3`, `(t₁, x₁, y₁) = (50, 0.31, 0.03)`, `(t₂, x₂, y₂) = (60, 0.305, 0.025)`, the direct and closed forms agree to `10^{−15}` and `|a|² − |b|² = 1.0000000000`.

tests.name: theDataAtA
tests.statement: The data at a single time satisfy (2.2): `E Ẽ# − Ẽ E# = 2i` at `s` exactly when `cos Φ = √(w w̃)`.

tests.name: andNoMotionOf
tests.statement: `e = 0`: `b = 0` and `|a| = sinh 2υ/N = 1`; no motion of the resonance means no scattering at `s`.

targets.name: resonance_time_proportion_tendsto_zero
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s` and every `C > 0`, if `Iₙ(s)` is the longest subinterval of `[2ⁿ, 2ⁿ⁺¹]` such that `Q(s, C/t)` contains a zero of `E(t, ·)` for every `t ∈ Iₙ(s)`, then `|Iₙ(s)|/2ⁿ → 0` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 9 line 1350–1377; mauth2022 §3.3 Corollary 7 line 1525 for the analogous half-line statement). Route: if the set of `s` with `lim sup |Iₙ(s)|/2ⁿ > 2/m` had positive measure, then for infinitely many `n` a set `Sₙ` of measure `≳ |Zₙ|/m`, `Zₙ = {s : |Iₙ(s)| > 2ⁿ/m}`, shares a time `t₁` in the middle thirds of the `Iₙ(s)`; with `t₂ = t₁ + 2ⁿ/(3m)`, §9.2 and §8.8–§8.9 give `log|a_{t₁→t₂}| ≥ c_m > 0` on `ℝ ∩ Q(s, C/2ⁿ⁺¹)` for `s ∈ Sₙ`; a cover of index two and §9.1's Plancherel identity give `|Zₙ| ≲_{m,C} ‖f‖²_{L²(2ⁿ, 2ⁿ⁺¹)}`, which is summable, and Borel–Cantelli concludes.

tests.name: compactSupportTheResonances
tests.statement: Compact support: the resonances are fixed (§8 Examples), so `Iₙ(s) = ∅` for large `n`.

tests.name: summabilityInput
tests.statement: Summability input: `Σₙ ‖f‖²_{L²(2ⁿ, 2ⁿ⁺¹)} = ‖f‖²_{L²(1, ∞)} < ∞`.

tests.name: aResonanceAtFixed
tests.statement: A resonance at fixed distance `δ` from `s` lies in `Q(s, C/t)` only for `t ≤ C/δ`, so it contributes to `Iₙ(s)` only for `2ⁿ ≤ C/δ`.

targets.name: insertZeroInterval
targets.statement: For `t₁ ≥ 0` and `β ≥ 0` define `f^{t₁,β}` as `f` on `[0, t₁)`, `0` on `[t₁, t₁ + β)` and `f(· − β)` on `[t₁ + β, ∞)`, and write `*` for its data (poltoratski2024 line 1380–1388). Its API:

api.name: forWithTheFree
api.statement: For `t ≥ t₁`, `M*(t + β, z) = M_{t₁→t}(z) M₀(β, z) M(t₁, z)` with `M₀` the free fundamental matrix; in particular `E*(t₁ + β, z) = e^{−iβz} E(t₁, z)` and `Ẽ*(t₁ + β, z) = e^{−iβz} Ẽ(t₁, z)`.

api.name: theSubintervalDataOf
api.statement: The subinterval data of `f^{t₁,β}` on `(t₁ + β, t₂ + β)` equal those of `f` on `(t₁, t₂)`, and `‖f^{t₁,β}‖ = ‖f‖`.

api.name: exactIncrementRelationIn
api.statement: Exact increment relation: in the setting of §9.2, if `E*(t₂ + β, s)` and `Ẽ*(t₂ + β, s)` have the forms of §9.2 with the same `w, w̃, Φ`, then the forms at `t₁ + β` hold with `υ* = υ` and `α₁* = e^{−iβs} α₁`, and `sin e*/sin(e* + 2iυ) = e^{2iβs} sin e/sin(e + 2iυ)` (poltoratski2024 (9.5)–(9.8) line 1400–1481).

api.name: routeTheChainRule
api.statement: Route: the chain rule; `E′ = −izE` on the inserted interval; the translation rule (§5.6) for the segment's transform, and §9.2 on both sides.

tests.name: andTheIdentityIs
tests.statement: `β = 0`: `f^{t₁,0} = f`, `e* = e`, and the identity is trivial.

tests.name: choiceOfAsRuns
tests.statement: Choice of `β`: as `β` runs over an interval of length `π/|s|` (`s ≠ 0`), `e^{2iβs}` runs once around the unit circle, which is how the argument of `e*` is adjusted (poltoratski2024 line 1479–1481, 1518–1520).

tests.name: soSPlancherelIdentity
tests.statement: `‖f^{t₁,β}‖_{L²(t₁+β, t₂+β)} = ‖f‖_{L²(t₁, t₂)}`, so §9.1's Plancherel identity is the same for both segments.

targets.name: sinh_ratio_gap
targets.statement: For `υ > 0` put `F_υ(x) = sinh x/sinh(υ + x)`. Prove that there are `c(υ) > 0` and `Δ₀(υ) > 0` such that for `0 < Δ < Δ₀` and `Δ₁, Δ₂ ∈ (0, 3Δ)` with `|F_υ(Δ₁) − sinh Δ/sinh(υ − Δ)| ≤ c(υ)Δ³/8` and `|F_{υ+Δ₁}(Δ₂) − sinh Δ/sinh(υ − 2Δ)| ≤ c(υ)Δ³/8`, one has `|sinh 2Δ/sinh(υ − 2Δ) − sinh(Δ₁ + Δ₂)/sinh(υ + Δ₁ + Δ₂)| ≥ c(υ)Δ²` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 10 line 1584–1663). Route: expand `F_υ(x) = x/S − Cx²/S² + O(x³)` with `S = sinh υ`, `C = cosh υ`; then `Δ₁ = Δ + 2CΔ²/S + O(Δ³)`, `Δ₂ = Δ + 4CΔ²/S + O(Δ³)`, and the difference is `2CΔ²/S² + O(Δ³)`.
hypotheses: 0 < Δ < Δ₀(υ), Δ₁, Δ₂ ∈ (0, 3Δ) with the two near-equalities

tests.name: withExactHypothesesThe
tests.statement: With exact hypotheses, the ratio of the difference to `Δ²` at `υ = 1` is `2.4204`, `2.3250`, `2.2792` for `Δ = 0.02, 0.01, 0.005`, tending to `2 cosh 1/sinh² 1 ≈ 2.2346`; at `υ = 0.5` it tends to `8.305`, at `υ = 2` to `0.572`.

tests.name: atAgainstTheExpansion
tests.statement: `Δ₁ = 0.010270` at `υ = 1`, `Δ = 0.01`, against the expansion `0.010263`.

tests.name: theLowerBoundFails
tests.statement: The lower bound fails without the quadratic term: the first-order terms cancel (`2Δ/S` on both sides).

targets.name: eventually_no_resonance_in_box
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s ∈ ℝ` and every `C > 0` there is `T(s, C)` such that `Q(s, C/t)` contains no zero of `E(t, ·)` for `t > T(s, C)`; hence there is `C(t) → ∞` with `Q(s, C(t)/t)` free of zeros for large `t` (poltoratski2024 §9 line 1173–1539: "Special case", "General case" and "Final step"). Route: if not, by §9.3 a resonance near `s` enters and leaves the box `Q(s, 2C/t)` infinitely often and moves by a hyperbolic distance comparable to a fixed small `Δ`; for three times `t₁ < t₂ < t₃` with purely vertical increments `e = τ = iΔ` (the special case), inserting zero intervals (§9.4) makes the modified increments purely imaginary, `e* = −iΔ₁`, `τ* = −iΔ₂`, and comparing moduli on `(t₁, t₂)`, `(t₂, t₃)` and `(t₁, t₃)` gives the three relations of §9.5, whose conclusion contradicts the third relation; the general case is reduced to the special one by two insertions with `β₁`, `β₂` chosen through §9.4 and a continuity argument in `t₂`; the errors of §8.8–§8.9 are taken `≪ Δ⁴`.

locator.where: §9 line 1173–1539 (special case, general case, final step)

tests.name: compactSupportTheResonances
tests.statement: Compact support: the resonances are fixed zeros of `E(T, ·)` at positive distance from `ℝ`, so the conclusion holds for every `s`.

tests.name: freeCaseNoZeros
tests.statement: Free case: no zeros at all.

tests.name: notSquareIntegrableFor
tests.statement: `f ≡ c` (not square-integrable): for `s ∈ (−c, c)`, `|E(t, s)|` grows like `e^{√(c² − s²) t}`, and the conclusion of §9.7, which follows from this one, fails there; the almost-everywhere statement needs `f ∈ L²`.

targets.name: diracE_asymptotics_ae
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s` and every `D > 0` there are unimodular `α(s, t)` and a constant `β(s)` with `Im β(s) = −√(w(s) w̃(s))`, `|β(s)| = 1`, such that `sup_{Q(s,D/t)} |E(t, z) + iα(s, t) e^{−itz}/√w(s)| → 0` and `sup_{Q(s,D/t)} |Ẽ(t, z) + iβ(s) α(s, t) e^{−itz}/√w̃(s)| → 0`; consequently `|E(t, s)| → 1/√w(s)`, `|Ẽ(t, s)| → 1/√w̃(s)`, `|a(t, s)|² → (1/w + 1/w̃ + 2)/4` and `|b(t, s)|² → (1/w + 1/w̃ − 2)/4` at `s` (poltoratski2024 (9.9)–(9.10) line 1538–1574). Route: §9.6 and §8.7(2) for `E` and for `Ẽ`; (2.2) on `ℝ` gives `(conj β − β)/√(w w̃) = 2i`.

tests.name: inTheLimitBy
tests.statement: `|b|² ≥ 0` in the limit: `1/w + 1/w̃ ≥ 2/√(w w̃) ≥ 2` by the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality and `w w̃ ≤ 1` (§6.5); and `|a|² − |b|² → 1`.

tests.name: compactSupportAtFor
tests.statement: Compact support at `x = 0` for `f = c 1_{[0,T]}`: `w(0) = e^{−2cT}`, `w̃(0) = e^{2cT}`, and the limit `|a|² = (e^{2cT} + e^{−2cT} + 2)/4 = cosh² cT` is the exact value `a(T, 0) = cosh cT`.

targets.name: nlft_truncate_tendsto_ae
targets.statement: Prove that for every real square-integrable `f`, `b(T, s)/a(T, s) = (f_T)⌃*(s) → f⌃*(s)` as `T → ∞` for almost every `s ∈ ℝ`; the strong form: for almost every `s` and every `C > 0`, `sup_{|z − s| < C/T} |(f_T)⌃(z) − f⌃*(s)| → 0`, where `(f_T)⌃ = b(T, ·)/a(T, ·)` is holomorphic on the disc for large `T`; and the corollaries: `a(T, s)`, `b(T, s)` have convergent moduli, and the generalised eigenfunctions `t ↦ M(t, s)` are bounded on `[0, ∞)` for almost every `s` (poltoratski2024 Theorem 1 line 578–586 and line 54–57; mauth2022 Theorem 2 line 216 and Theorem 6 line 4121 for the equivalence with the absence of resonances). Route: §9.7 makes `b/a = (E − iẼ)/(E + iẼ)` uniformly close on `Q(s, D/T)` to the constant `(1/√w − iβ/√w̃)/(1/√w + iβ/√w̃)`, so the pointwise limit exists almost everywhere; §5.5 gives `(f_T)⌃* → f⌃*` in `Π`-measure, so along a subsequence almost everywhere, and the two limits agree almost everywhere.

locator.where: Theorem 1 line 578–586 and line 54–57; mauth2022 Theorem 2 line 216, Theorem 6 line 4121

tests.name: integrableTheConvergenceIs
tests.statement: `f` integrable: the convergence is uniform on `ℝ` (§5.2), with no exceptional set.

tests.name: compactSupportFor
tests.statement: Compact support: `(f_T)⌃* = f⌃*` for `T ≥ T₀`.

tests.name: boundedEigenfunctionsFailWithout
tests.statement: Bounded eigenfunctions fail without square-integrability: `f ≡ c` at `s ∈ (−c, c)` has `M(t, s)` growing like `e^{√(c² − s²) t}`.

tests.name: freeCaseAndFor
tests.statement: Free case: `f⌃ = 0` and `b(T, ·) = 0` for every `T`.
